dimensions concern the coefficient fibre, not the arithmetic fibre or $\Oz$ (\cref{osq:rm:sub:cyclic}).
Nor do the eighth-batch additions. 24's maximal ideals exist in $\mathsf{GBC}$, not in the base theory of \cref{osq:sub:foundations}; they are
defined relative to a global well-order, not canonically, their membership may be undecidable, and neither the maximal ideals above $1+\omega^a$ nor
their residue fields are classified: the branching count $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a lower bound, and the residue fields embed in $\SC$ without being
identified with it (\cref{osq:cr:sub:residues}). 25 classifies the globally smooth semialgebraic preservers only; finitely smooth and nonsmooth ones
are controlled on their tails, not on bounded intervals, and its sampling theorem excludes coefficient-independent tests, not coefficient-adapted
certificates (\cref{osq:sa:sub:semialgebraic}). 26 computes flat dimensions of the geometric radical quotients of set-sized cone cores, not their
projective dimensions in general, not arbitrary ideals and not any dimension of $\Oz$, and its flat dimensions do not transfer to $\Oz$, the passage
being nonflat (\cref{osq:pc:sub:polyhedral}). 27's henselization and spectra are those of set-sized local rings $\mathfrak L$ of its hulls, not of $\Oz$;
it counts the minimal primes and the generic branches but does not classify the Stone space or the Boolean algebra (\cref{osq:hb:sub:henselian}).

As an internal ring, $\Oz$ has all surreal scales available through its fraction field, a nonzero
proper-class ideal $\Pi$, nonzero class-valued derivations and nonarithmetic prime quotients; as a
source of representations on sets it carries no more scalar information than $\Z$. The gap is caused
not by ignoring limits but by finite identities that become available once the source contains the
appropriate Hahn sums (06). Adapting 06's list of hypotheses that must remain visible to all the
constructions, the proofs use four different size restrictions, each for its own reason: individual supports are sets, so that a common positive gap exists; the full class of smaller
scales supplies arbitrarily large collision families; in the set-sized models an uncountable bound
admits the countable witnesses, and regularity (or cofinality, or the finite-coordinate invariant)
bounds unions of fewer than the relevant number of supports; and cardinal arithmetic enters only in
computing the size of the ring, which is the exact threshold. Dropping any of them needs a new
argument: finite supports lack the witnesses (\cref{osq:sec:support}), full supports over a fixed set
group need not have gaps (\cref{osq:rem:fstar}), and singular support bounds may preserve field closure
but not the simultaneous gap property.

\subsection{Non-claims of the sources}\label{osq:sub:nonclaims}
Every limitation stated by a source survives. They are listed and numbered by source;
several recur in the text where the corresponding result is proved.

\paragraph{03.} (1) Not peer reviewed; no Lean declarations. (2) ``Developed here'' is relative to the
inspected material; no certified priority. (3) Neither Conway's general refinement problem nor the general factorization problems for omnific
integers are settled.
(4) No classification of exponent groups or support restrictions; the cardinal theorem is a
realization theorem for its family. (5) $\cf\kappa=\aleph_0$ is excluded. (6) Only the lower bound
$\mu$ on the number of algebra generators of $\NN_\kappa$ is proved. (7) No complete integrality test
for mixed supports. (8) No descent equality $\NN\cap F^{03}_\kappa=\NN_\kappa$ (the equality holds by
\cref{osq:bb:cor:descent03}, a merge result from 20's support projection). (9) No statement on
proper-class-valued valuations. (10) Infinite set-sized images of the normalizations are not
classified, and the absence of finite images is a general consequence of containing the real
algebraic integers (19 has since classified the domain images, \cref{osq:nf:thm:domainimages}; images
with zero divisors remain unclassified). (11) No class tensor products and no class prime-ideal theorem; all $\Tor$ is over
set-sized rings. (12) The finite checks do not verify the cardinal or class arguments. (13) Restricted
Hahn fields, truncation integer parts, complete-integral-closure terminology and the small-unit lemma
are standard or elementary, with no priority claim; Kuhlmann is context only. (14) The full-class
theorem, common divisors and clearing are credited to the companion manuscript (05). (15) Density produces no convergent set-indexed net: every set-generated intermediate algebra is
uniformly discrete, so the dense normalization needs more than any set of generators. (16)
$\tfrac12\NN[i]$ is not asserted to be a ring. (17) The flatness result is an application of standard
module theory, not a new general flatness theorem. (18) Density does not impose continuity on abstract
ring homomorphisms. (19) No claim about unrestricted surcomplex analytic continuation is made.

\paragraph{04.} (1) Unrefereed; no Lean formalization; the universal theorems are candidate
contributions without certified priority. (2) No classification of all class ideals, no class Zorn
argument, no claim that proper class ideals extend to maximal ones (24 has since proved the extension with global choice,
\cref{osq:cr:thm:krull}; batch 34). (3) The module equivalence covers
set-sized modules only, not class modules, group representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\Oz)$, or
additive homomorphisms. (4) It does not say that $P(\ct(x))=0$ implies $P(x)=0$. (5) It does not
classify infinite points of curves; the earlier project's curve questions are not declared solved.
(6) Nothing is inferred about fraction fields of the bounded-support rings. (7) The fixed-workspace
results are lower bounds only. (8) No named open conjecture is solved. (9) Additive coefficient maps
escape the theorem and are not counterexamples. (10) The telescope has a direct precursor
\cite[Remark~3.4.4]{LM}; the constant term, finite quotients and common shifts come from the prior
manuscript (02 of \cite{RepoOdg}). (11) The existence of standard part is classical and in the
repository's infrastructure. (12) The support-threshold theorem differs from fixed-group completion or
omitted-type questions. (13) The finite checks do not prove normal forms, infinite identities, class
factorizations or novelty. (14) The quotient, module, derivation and localization results are a
connected theorem package deduced from the universal theorems, not unrelated discoveries.

\paragraph{06.} (1) Unrefereed, not Lean-verified; priority not established by the targeted searches.
(2) $\pd\Z$ is shown only to be at least $2$. (3) Residue fields of nonarithmetic primes are not
classified; the prime-reservoir proposition is a necessary condition, not an existence theorem.
(4) The primality of $\omega^{\sqrt2}+\omega+1$ is imported; no factorization, refinement, GCD or
unique-factorization conjecture is used or claimed. (5) No automorphisms, class ideals or factorization
patterns are described. (6) No elementarity claim for $A^{06}_\kappa\subseteq\Oz$; no compactness
argument for a proper-class theory. (7) The Euler derivation is not asserted to be the
Berarducci--Mantova derivation or compatible with exponentiation. (8) Real closedness of
bounded-support Hahn fields is not a novelty claim, and regularity is not claimed necessary for field
closure. (9) The idea of a universal set-sized quotient is not new to the repository. (10) The module
correspondence is not a Morita equivalence of unrestricted module theories. (11) The invisible prime
quotient does not say that a particular maximal class ideal fails to exist. (12) The polynomial-test
theorem does not assert that a proper-class coordinate ring defines an ordinary scheme. (13) The
finite-congruence observation is elementary and not a strong novelty claim. (14) Numerical tests and a
successful build are not proofs; the formalization route was not executed.

\paragraph{07.} (1) Conway's refinement conjecture is neither settled nor used (the Abramov
development \cite{Abramov} is cited for its claim and caveats only); no historical priority; no referee;
no Lean. (2) The Cantor algebra is a specified subalgebra; neither the idempotents nor the prime ideals
of $\Qa_a$ are classified, and $\Qa_a$ is not claimed to be a function ring. (3) The statement on
nonarithmetic primes is conditional; no existence is asserted (24 has since proved existence with global choice, \cref{osq:cr:thm:binomialmax};
batch 34). (4) Surreal self-similarity is credited
to Bagayoko--van der Hoeven. (5) $\Theta_a$ is not claimed to preserve the ordinal embedding,
birthdays, simplicity or the exponential; $\vartheta$ is not additive and $\Psi$ not multiplicative.
(6) Quotient, completion and module classifications are consequences, not separate major discoveries.
(7) The small-image theorem does not say that no set-valued invariant sees positive exponents. (8) The
module equivalence is not a homological-dimension statement over class modules. (9) The global theorem
is not a theorem about small approximations of $\Oz$. (10) The finite checks do not verify the
transfinite or ambient-support arguments. (11) The CRT isomorphisms at different stages need not be
coherent; evaluation at a point of $\Z_2$ is not claimed to extend to $\Qa_a$ (with global choice it extends to a map onto a larger
field, \cref{osq:cr:rem:evaluation}; batch 34); no topology on $\EE_a$
is used. (12) Class prime ideals are not classified, and no Zorn argument for a proper class of
ideals is used (24 has since shown, with global choice and a recursion on elements rather than a Zorn argument, that maximal class ideals
exist, \cref{osq:cr:thm:krull}; they are still not classified; batch 34). (13) No exponential function on surcomplex arguments is assumed.

\paragraph{08.} (1) Candidate-original, not certified priority, not refereed, no Lean; the broad
factorization questions for $\Oz$ are not addressed. (2) $\Frac(A^{08}_\kappa)=F^{08}_\kappa$ is not
claimed. (3) Residue-field isomorphism types are not classified. (4) No closure under derivations or
exponentials, no initial-segment or birthday condition on the embedding. (5) The collision mechanism
has published precedents (\cite[Proposition~8.2.1]{LM}); the constant retraction and finite reductions
are not principal novelty claims. (6) Fixed Hahn workspaces lie outside the theorem (an Archimedean group has no
small scales at all). (7) The non-integral-closure corollary is not a factorization theorem. (8) Class-sized modules
are not classified; the theorem is not an isomorphism with $\Z$, and individual monomials can be
represented faithfully in small rings. (9) The Hahn derivations $D_\eta$ are not an
exponential-compatible calculus. (10) No maximal-ideal theorem for proper-class rings; no assertion that
proper class ideals lie in maximal ones (24 has since proved one with global choice, \cref{osq:cr:thm:krull}; batch 34). (11) The quantitative criterion gives sufficient conditions
only. (12) The finite checks prove neither the class theorem, nor summability, nor real closedness.
(13) The primality of $\omega^{\sqrt2}+\omega+1$ is an imported published theorem.

\paragraph{09.} (1) Novelty provisional after a targeted comparison; no referee; no proof-assistant
verification. (2) No named factorization conjecture solved; primality imported. (3) The number of
maximal ideals and the isomorphism types of the residue fields of $A^{09}_{\lambda,D}$ are not
determined. (4) No assertion about the unrestricted (uncountable-support) ring over
$\Gamma^{09}_\lambda$. (5) No class Zorn argument; the Jacobson statements concern set-sized rings.
(6) $\GOz$ is a subring of the surcomplex field, not the field. (7) The checks do not verify infinite
supports, cardinal arithmetic or the existence of maximal ideals. (8) The geometric identity is
elementary with precedents; profinite, derivation and flatness statements are consequences; the
Gaussian $2$-torsion computation is standard. (9) No global surcomplex exponential, sine, integration or
topology is used; the arithmetic quotient is not an ordered quotient. (10) The rotation quotient is a
conceptual predecessor, not imported. (11) No new exponential derivation is constructed and no
uniqueness of the Berarducci--Mantova derivation is claimed. (12) $I/I^2=0$ is not a
finite-presentation or smoothness claim.

\paragraph{10.} (1) Unrefereed and not machine-checked; targeted review only; no named factorization
conjecture solved. (2) For $r\ge1$ the $p$-adic completion is not a profinite completion. (3) No
classification of all class ideals, automorphisms or factorizations. (4) No transfer principle from
$\Z$ to $\Oz$. (5) $\Int(\Z[i]^r)$ is not replaced by a binomial basis. (6) The derivation $D_h$ is not the
Berarducci--Mantova derivation. (7) The universe-relative reading must carry the size restriction in
its statement. (8) The rational classification is not a classification of arbitrary functions or of
coordinatewise conjugation. (9) The congruence theorem does not make reduction modulo an infinite
omnific integer an ordinary finite congruence, and does not classify congruence-preserving class
functions. (10) Classical ingredients (Newton interpolation, binomial rings, the least-common-multiple
pattern, $p$-adic approximation) are credited, not claimed. (11) The grid test assumes exact surreal
input; no effective encoding is claimed. (12) The finite checks do not test class functions, support
lemmas or priority.

\paragraph{11.} (1) The main theorem is relative to one fixed universe, not to fragments viewed in a
larger universe. (2) No classification of prime or maximal class ideals. (3) No class module of
K\"ahler differentials. (4) The presentation theorem is not quantifier elimination or a
reconstruction of class-valued solutions. (5) Sharpness of the coinitiality theorem is stated under
$\kappa^{<\kappa}=\kappa$ and $|K|\le\kappa$ as explicit extra assumptions (the unconditional value is a
merge result, \cref{osq:prop:card11}). (6) Necessary closure conditions for intermediate rings are not
given. (7) The ordinal answer is not claimed hard or unknown to specialists. (8) Bounded-support
coefficient rings and lower-scale geometric division have precedents in \cite[Section~8]{LM}.
(9) Targeted novelty assessment only; the finite checks prove no infinite-support or class-size
statement. (10) The rotation-group theme is acknowledged, not originated. (11) The only answer to
the MathOverflow question concerns transcendence degree. (12) No primality or refinement conjecture is
newly settled; the ideals, class-valued representations and factorization theory of quotients invisible
to set-sized rings are not determined, and ordinary factorization questions about $\Oz$ remain
outside the conclusions.

\paragraph{12.} (1) Nothing is claimed about the homological dimensions of the full proper-class ring $\Oz$; all
rings are set-sized and all embeddings use finite normal forms. (2) The weak global dimension of $A_d$ is not computed;
only the lower bound $d+1$ is proved. (3) Projective dimensions are given only as bounds (the exact values in rank one
are merge results; 21 has since determined them for every $d$, \cref{osq:da:cor:exactpd,osq:da:thm:lattice}). (4) Arbitrary non-simplicial cones, arbitrary ideals and all homological localizations of the cores
are not classified (26 has since computed the flat dimensions of radical monomial quotients over every rational polyhedral cone,
\cref{osq:pc:sub:polyhedral}; batch 34). (5) The cores are not integer parts of $\No$, not initial in the simplicity order, not preserved by
all surreal automorphisms and not Hahn rings; the countable-rank ring still consists of finite sums. (6) $\widehat A$ is
the profinite completion, not a Hahn completion or a completion in a surreal-valued topology. (7) The $D+M$ framework
(with the pullback literature, for instance \cite{WKX}), filtered-colimit flatness, coherence criteria and the
idempotent-kernel mechanism of formal \'etaleness are classical and credited; the proposed contributions are the
Boolean $\Tor$ computation, its dimension consequences, the countable-rank realization and the ordered-cone comparison.
(8) No named conjecture is claimed solved; the originality check was targeted, not an exhaustive priority audit.
(9) Not refereed and not checked in Lean. (10) The finite audit uses $\Q\subset\Q(\sqrt2)$ on a five-point grid and proves
nothing over $\Z$ or for all exponents. (11) The Gaussian version uses only the quadratic extension $\SC$; no analytic
continuation and no topology on a proper class is used. (12) ``Nilpotent'' is a test condition on algebras; the cores are
domains.

\paragraph{13.} (1) The theorems are relative to size; nothing is claimed about all maps out of a fixed set-sized Hahn
ring, whose identity is a counterexample ($\Z+X\R[X]$ with evaluation at $1$ is 13's example). (2) No classification of
class quotients, class residue objects or class ideals, and no maximal-ideal theorem or Zorn argument for class rings.
(3) The ordinal result answers only the quotient addendum; the original transcendence-degree question has Wofsey's
answer; 13's priority as a first answer is not established. (4) The integer divisibility of the purely infinite part is
known (L'Innocente--Mantova); equation-only transfer along a retraction, filtered-colimit flatness and the algebra of
idempotent quotient ideals are standard, and the homological and lifting statements are standard consequences, with no
\'etaleness claimed under finite presentation. (5) The fiber theorem (printed in \cite{RepoOdg}) classifies only nonzero
fibers of decomposable polynomials; there is no general classification of fibers, no Thue or Baker finiteness, and no
enumeration of the ordinary solutions of its cubic. (6) The cardinal criterion is a necessary condition, not an existence
theorem for detecting maps. (7) The statement on Hilbert's tenth problem is a transfer of the classical theorem, with no
complexity claim for Gaussian or number-field problems. (8) No claim about Conway's refinement conjecture; no refinement,
primality or unique-factorization property is used. (9) In the two-universe reading ``not generated by a set'' means not
generated by a family from the smaller universe. (10) Unrefereed; no Lean; the finite checks verify identities only; the
literature and repository searches were bounded, and the repository was neither audited nor built.

\paragraph{14.} (1) Arbitrary finitely generated omnific ideals, with generators at several support levels, are not
classified. (2) The rank-one modules with double dual $B$ are not all listed. (3) No coefficient ring other than a
principal ideal domain is treated. (4) The exact weak global dimension of $A_0$ is not claimed. (5) The ideal-class group
under $\odot$ is not a subgroup of $\operatorname{Pic}(A)$, and its identity is $L(\mathfrak o)$, not $A$. (6) Full-class
tensor products are explicit carriers only, and ordinary flat dimensions are asserted only over $A_0$. (7) No novelty is
attached to noncoherence; the $D+M$ context is credited to Dobbs--Papick, and no valuation-ring hypothesis is used.
(8) The number field spanned by a multiplier ring need not be totally real. (9) The unimodular-direction criterion
concerns coordinate representatives, not all points of a projective scheme over a ring, and its example $[1:\sqrt2]$ is
not new. (10) The matrix theorem concerns constant matrices at one common monomial scale. (11) Constant-term arithmetic,
flat idempotent support ideals and cardinal obstructions are credited to companion manuscripts and are not presented as
new. (12) No Conway factorization or refinement claim; no peer review and no new Lean verification; priority is
provisional; the finite checks are supplementary and certify no arbitrary support, class universal property, flatness
statement or Eisenstein criterion in all degrees.

\paragraph{15.} (1) The main theorem is for the full class only; the finite-support ring and fixed Hahn workspaces are
counterexamples. (2) Its local cardinal criterion is sufficient only. (3) No classification of class prime or maximal
ideals; its prime classification carries a set-sized residue hypothesis. (4) The primality of $\omega^{\sqrt2}+\omega+1$ is
imported from L'Innocente--Mantova and is not a new solution of Gonshor's question. (5) No claim about Conway's refinement
problem; the repository \texttt{gaearon/conway-refinement} was noticed but neither built, audited nor relied on. (6) Only
set-sized modules are classified; this is not a Morita statement. (7) Universe parameters must stay separate.
(8) Geometric factorization and the congruence calculations are classical or elementary, the categorical deductions are
not new techniques, and the rotation-group theorem is a precedent, not a dependency. (9) Blocking one extension of the
finite-support augmentation is weaker than the theorem. (10) Embeddings of set-sized rings into $\Oz$ are not excluded,
and $\Oz$ and $\Z$ are not claimed to have the same first-order theory. (11) Candidate originality rests on a bounded
search; no referee; no Lean; the checks cover finite identities only.

\paragraph{16.} (1) Rational-to-polynomial collapse is not new in principle (D-rings: Gunji--McQuillan, as recalled by
Liu; related framework in \cite{CFMT}). (2) Surjectivity rigidity covers one variable and rational functions only;
conjugation, multivariate triangular bijections, class functions, definable maps and formal power series are excluded,
and not every bijection of $\Oz$ is claimed affine. (3) The fresh-scale arguments do not transfer to a fixed Hahn field
without dominant exponents. (4) The certificates are relative to exact coefficient data, zero tests and a certificate of
freshness; they are not a decision procedure for arbitrary surreal inputs. (5) No convergence, analytic continuation,
surreal exponential, Berarducci--Mantova derivation, fine-topological completeness or factorization is used. (6) Newton
interpolation and binomial bases are classical, and the Gaussian test is not claimed minimal. (7) The fiber theorem
classifies the particular fresh fiber, not every fiber. (8) Priority rests on a bounded search; no referee; no Lean; the
finite checks are not proofs.

\paragraph{17.} (1) No Lean formalization and no peer review; no named factorization conjecture is resolved, and no factorization
property is inferred from noncoherence. (2) The kernel theorem classifies constant matrices after one common monomial scaling, not
matrices with several leading scales or positive tails; ideals not of the form $J_g(M)$ are not classified. (3) No upper bound on the
weak global dimension of $R^{11}_\kappa$, no global dimension, and no projective dimension of $\Pi^{11}_\kappa$ or $J_g(M)$ is claimed (the
last two are asked); Dobbs's valuation-pullback theorem does not apply because $K+\Pi^{11}_\kappa$ is not a valuation ring. (4) The
power-growth law counts generators only; the lattices $M^n$ need not stabilize when their ranks do, and it is not a reconstruction
theorem. (5) Over the class ring, $\Hom$ means scalar codes, not a class of class maps; ordinary $\Tor$, flat resolutions and weak
dimensions are taken over set-sized models only, and no full-class $\Tor$ is inferred from the statement on modules killed by the
tail. (6) Neither inversion closure of $R^{11}_\kappa$ nor its equality with a Hahn field is asserted; nothing is said about unrestricted
Hahn series over an arbitrary divisible group, and the coinitiality of the positive cone is not the cofinality of the group. (7) The
appendix proof of the universal theorem is background, not a novelty candidate. (8) The $D+M$ noncoherence mechanism and the relation
module $M^{r-1}$ are classical (Dobbs, Dobbs--Papick); the pullback literature may contain antecedents of the $\Hom$ and tensor formulas;
the audit of the repository and of the literature was targeted, not exhaustive. (9) The rank algorithm assumes an exact description
of the coefficient span, not floating-point data. (10) The checks are finite arithmetic; kernel bases computed over $\Q$ are not
integral lattice bases, and no proper-class argument, regularity statement, Hahn support or homological theorem is checked. (11) A
field $\Frac(D)M$ in the field test does not make $M$ a ring. (12) The support-gap argument does not transfer to unrestricted Hahn series
with real exponents.

\paragraph{18.} (1) The dichotomy is one-variable: $XY$ defeats any bound in several variables, only the linewise statement is proved,
and how the exceptional cosets on different lines fit together is open. (2) The coefficient test is an algebraic certificate relative to
exact coefficient operations, not an algorithm for arbitrary surreal representations. (3) Rational collapse is not new (D-rings:
Gunji--McQuillan, recalled by Liu); the description of the integer-valued polynomials and the matrix and jet reductions are applications,
and the all-size matrix test is a general algebraic observation. (4) Finite testing concerns polynomials of known degree only; no finite
sample tests rational functions, and entire Hahn series and nonstandard degrees are excluded (for entire series see the batch-32
status note after \cref{osq:or:cor:workspace}). (5) The Gaussian simplex test is not
claimed minimal; the results of Volkov and Petrov are classical input. (6) Surjections are classified among rational maps of one
variable only, not arbitrary bijections, automorphisms of the surreal field or polynomial automorphisms in several variables;
injectivity alone is weaker. (7) Nothing is claimed about $\No$ or the finite surreals, where the discrete gap fails, and no
factorization conjecture is addressed. (8) The checks cover finite-support models $\Q[H]$ and $\Q(i)[H]$ only and prove neither the cluster
lemma, nor the proper-class reading, nor novelty. (9) Novelty rests on a bounded search; no referee; no Lean. (10) The sharp examples need
an infinite element, and for a general discretely ordered ring finite testability of preservation must not be assumed.

\paragraph{19.} (1) $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$ is not determined: its size, its atoms, whether it is trivial and whether it is a set (20 has since
shown that it is nontrivial, atomless and a proper class, \cref{osq:bb:thm:atoms}; its isomorphism type is still not determined). (2) There is no
membership criterion for $\NN$ by normal forms (20 adds support descent and the one-scale rational case, \cref{osq:bb:thm:descent,osq:bb:thm:rational},
but no general criterion). (3) $\mathsf B_\bullet$ is neither one finite product nor an unrestricted product of copies of
$\overline\Z$. (4) The real-case coefficient embedding depends on the choice of $\mathsf v$; no embedding of $\C$ into $\No$ is asserted. (5) No
B\'ezout property of $\Oz$ or of the normalizations is claimed. (6) The characteristic-$p$ fibres are neither reduced nor fields; the mod-2
splitting is a product of nonreduced rings. (7) Set-sized images with zero divisors are classified only up to the factorization through
$\mathsf B_\bullet$; not all set-sized images are claimed countable; $\mathsf B_\bullet$ is not asserted to be a set (20 has since proved it a proper
class), and no universal object in a category of set-sized rings is claimed. (8) The kernel detection uses an explicit foundation (class theory with global choice, no class
Zorn lemma, no measurable cardinals), and its intersections are pointwise kernel characterizations, not sets of class maps. (9) In the
finite-axiom form, $\upsilon_T$ need not be infinitesimal, non-set-generation needs the full class, the small-image theorem needs a cardinal
condition absent from the axioms, and nothing transfers to a fixed Hahn field, where the support $\{1/n\}$ blocks the monomial proof
without being a counterexample (20's reduced-fibre result, \cref{osq:bb:prop:fixedboolean}, avoids the axioms and decides no radicality;
23 has since shown that radicality fails in the cyclic workspace, which is outside the axioms, \cref{osq:rm:rem:fullclass}). (10) Integrality, absolute integral closure, Boolean powers and the B\'ezout property of $\overline\Z$ are
standard, and the small-image theorem is credited; priority is not established. (11) $\NN$ itself is not absolutely integrally closed,
lifted roots need not stay distinct modulo $\Pi\NN$, and norm-one units of the fibre are not asserted to lift. (12) No named factorization
conjecture is resolved; no referee; no Lean; the checks are finite identities and rational inequalities.

\paragraph{20.} (1) The class isomorphism type of $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$ is not determined: atomlessness and free subalgebras of every set size
do not make the class algebra free, complete or saturated for arbitrary Boolean types, and give no arbitrary infinite joins; no isomorphism
$\mathsf B_\R\cong\mathsf B_\R\times\mathsf B_\R$ is claimed (the proved doubling is $\mathsf B_\C\cong\mathsf B_\R\times\mathsf B_\R$). (2) The
fixed-workspace statements use $\sqrt{\Pi(G)\NN(G)}$; $\Pi(G)\NN(G)$ is not asserted radical in any fixed workspace, no atomlessness of
$\Idem(\mathsf C(G))$ for a fixed $G$ is asserted, and the rank extension needs a new dominant coordinate, which a fixed workspace need not
supply (23 has since decided both for every cyclic $G$, without a new coordinate: $\Pi(G)\NN(G)$ is not radical and $\Idem(\mathsf C(G))$ is
atomless, \cref{osq:rm:thm:explicit,osq:rm:cor:atomless}). (3) Support descent is not a decision algorithm; effective membership for general infinite supports is open, and the exact
rational criterion concerns one monomial scale. (4) The matrix corollary computes no projective or global dimension and forms no category of
class-sized modules; the higher projective dimensions of this report (\cref{osq:q:pd}) are not addressed. (5) $\sigma_\pm$ are specializations
of a finite branch algebra, not evaluations of Laurent series at $T=0$ or maps on the Laurent field; $\operatorname{pr}_G$ is linear, not a ring
retraction; no evaluation map on all surreal numbers is used. (6) An idempotent residue does not say that its representative is idempotent;
the quotient is not standard part. (7) The free algebra over an infinite index set is a directed union of finite products, not an
unrestricted product. (8) The foundation is class theory with global choice; no set of all class homomorphisms or prime class ideals is
formed, no set-sized Zorn argument is applied to a proper class, set-indexed families of class maps are single uniform class relations, and
statements about all maps are pointwise. (9) The coefficient copy of $\overline\Z$ is not canonical. (10) Radicality, saturation, the Boolean
power, integral doubling and domain-map detection are 19's and the small-image theorem is this report's, reproved and not claimed; general
Boolean powers, multiquadratic extensions, the determinant trick, coefficient projection as a module map and ultrafilter methods are not
new; it is not asserted that 19 was in the repository at 20's pin. (11) The questions resolved are those of 19, not a named conjecture; no
Gonshor prime-element, refinement or other named factorization problem is solved. (12) The source comparison was targeted; historical
priority is not established. (13) The finite checks verify polynomial identities, branch specializations, finite Boolean tables, finite support
projections and initial Laurent coefficients, not class or set arguments, Hahn support theorems, arbitrary supports, integrality of arbitrary
surreals or novelty. (14) No Lean formalization, no repository build, no peer review; Python and SymPy versions other than those recorded
(3.13.5 and 1.14.0) were not tested.

\paragraph{21.} (1) Unrefereed and AI-assisted; no Lean or other proof-assistant check; priority is not certified: the dimension question
is answered relative to the inspected repository version, the literature search was targeted, and unintegrated companion manuscripts and
historical sources were not exhaustively audited. (2) No major named factorization conjecture is claimed solved. (3) Arbitrary omnific
ideals are not classified. (4) The value $d+1$ concerns the specific set-sized core $A_d$, not $\pd\Z$ over the class ring; no exact global
or weak global dimension of $\Oz$ or of $A_d$ is claimed by 21; the stronger core lower bounds $d+2$ and $d+1$ use $K\ne\Frac D$. (5) The class rings are read under a
two-universe convention, not as literal proper-class rings of ordinary set theory; the core theorems and all examples are ordinary
set-sized mathematics. (6) The finite checks do not prove the infinite $\Ext$ nonvanishing, exactness in unbounded degree or the
normal-form foundations, and replace no proof assistant. (7) Filtered colimits of flat modules, flat models of derived tensor products,
countable telescopes (Positselski \cite{Positselski}) and the non-Noetherian dimension methods for root-adjoining rings (Asgharzadeh
\cite{Asgharzadeh}) are standard and not claimed. (8) The additive second-$\Tor$ formula is a dimension-shift consequence of the report's
tensor calculation, not an independent discovery; the flat face resolution, $\fd_{A_d}D=d$, the lattice syzygies and the tensor torsion are
the report's and are credited. (9) The $D$-module decomposition of $\Tor_1$ is not an $A$-module splitting. (10) The vanishing of $\Tor_2$
is not $\Tor$-independence ($\Tor_1\ne0$). (11) The disjointness test creates no field extensions and does not decide linear disjointness
without access to the arithmetic. (12) Reconstruction needs the boundary embedding and the distinguished $1$; an abstract $\Tor_2$ group, or
an abstract derived equivalence, is not claimed to recover an order. (13) The DGA model is not claimed cofibrant or $E_\infty$-formal, and
it determines no higher operations. (14) The minimal polynomial of an arbitrary element of degree at least three cannot be read from a
two-generator $\Tor_2$. (15) $\Tor_{>0}(D,E)=0$ for every module $E$ killed by the tail, despite $\pd D=d+1$; the nonvanishing uses the
target $A_d$. (16) On the finite-support core the augmentation to the coefficient field exists, so ``every set-sized target factors through
$\ct$'' is false there; the shadow theorem concerns the specified constant-term modules. (17) The resolutions control the specified face,
lattice and quotient modules, not all ideals; the length-two flat resolution and the $\Tor$ calculations are asserted for $T_\Q$ and the
class ring, not for $A_d$ with $d\ge2$, whose tail is not flat.

\paragraph{22.} (1) AI-assisted and unrefereed, with complete written arguments; no Lean build, no Wolfram computation and no independent referee
review. (2) No named longstanding conjecture is claimed settled; the finite-certificate and no-universal-set package is a proposed contribution, its
priority is not certified, and its novelty statement is a qualified assessment of selected material (and is incomplete, \cref{osq:sub:repository}).
(3) The bare collapse of integer-valued rational functions of one variable has the D-ring antecedent (Gunji--McQuillan, through Liu's
Proposition~1.12, the 1976 paper not read independently; the domain must be infinite), and the Newton basis and the binomial-ring viewpoint are
classical (Elliott \cite{ElliottBirings}, Cahen--Chabert \cite{CC}, the monograph not re-read in full); neither is claimed. (4) Normal forms, Hahn operations and $\Frac(\Oz)=\No$
(L'Innocente--Mantova, Proposition~2.4.5) and the repository's splitting, constant-term and fraction background are inherited; no unreviewed
geometric assertion of the repository is imported. (5) The certificates are relative to exact field operations and exact membership in $\Oz$ or
$\GOz$, not algorithms for arbitrary descriptions of surreal numbers; equality, gcd, support bounds and membership are not presumed decidable, and
choosing $b$ above an arbitrary support is a construction, not an effective operation. (6) Neither the rational bound
$(d+1)^m+m(2d^2+2d+1)^{m-1}$ nor the Gaussian grid is claimed optimal, and the anisotropic refinement is available only after the presentation has
been inspected. (7) The lower bound $(d+1)^m$ concerns fixed point-value tests chosen independently of the coefficients, not algorithms that inspect
the coefficients. (8) Point counts count exact evaluations, not bit operations or floating-point samples. (9) The no-set-test theorem needs the
full proper class and fails for set-sized rings; the fixed-workspace extension needs an available fresh exponent, and its failure for Archimedean
value groups is a failure of the method, not a proof that every finite test fails. (10) Arbitrary functions, entire Hahn series, surreal
exponentials, infinite-dimensional operators and Diophantine varieties are not classified (entire series preserving the omnific part of a
fixed workspace are classified in \cite{RepoEnt}; batch-32 status note after \cref{osq:or:cor:workspace}), nor are algebraic or semialgebraic maps ($|X|$ preserves
$\Oz$ and is only piecewise polynomial; 25 has since classified the globally $C^\infty$ semialgebraic ones, \cref{osq:sa:thm:smoothmany}, and shown
that finitely smooth ones need not be finitely piecewise polynomial, \cref{osq:sa:thm:bumps}; batch 34). (11) The birational corollary assumes a rational inverse in both directions; no bijective polynomial map is
claimed to have one, no Jacobian-conjecture claim is made, the coordinates need not have coefficients in $\Lambda$, and the automorphism group is not
classified. (12) Image ideals are not assumed principal, and no greatest-common-divisor conclusion is drawn. (13) The tensor isomorphisms are read
through finite sums of pure tensors or in a containing universe; they do not assert that $\Oz$ is a set. (14) Gaussian arithmetic is not replaced
by a Gaussian binomial basis; the ordinary Gaussian universal-set problem (Byszewski--Fr\k aczyk--Szumowicz \cite{BFS}, of which only the abstract and the
bibliographic record were inspected; Volkov--Petrov \cite{VP}) is neither solved nor presented as newly discovered. (15) $\omega^\gamma$ is the normal-form
monomial, not an analytic exponential; no algebraic closedness of $\SC$, differentiation or topology is used; $\ct$ is not a global standard part and
is multiplicative only on nonnegative supports. (16) The $1{,}776$ finite assertions (exact algebra and sampled lexicographic inequalities) verify no
arbitrary support, infinite Hahn summability, cut above an arbitrary set, class-sized quantifier, proper-class alternative or originality; the
lexicographic model illustrates the quantification over all exponents and does not replace it. (17) Only selected repository files were read, some
responses were truncated, the repository was neither checked out nor built, and an empty search was not taken as evidence of absence.
(18) Independent scrutiny may find simplifications, broader antecedents or errors.

\paragraph{23.} (1) The answers concern the cyclic exponent groups $\Z a$ only, for the real pair and its Gaussian counterpart; they classify neither
arbitrary ordered exponent groups nor support restrictions, and the proof does not classify the groups with a discrete convex component. (2) The Hahn
field over $\Q a$ is open; the Puiseux result concerns bounded denominators only, is not an identification with that Hahn field, and does not say
that the limit fibre is isomorphic to a reduced finite-stage fibre, whose image in it may grow. (3) The Boolean isomorphism types for $k=\R$ and $\C$
are not determined: the independent family does not make the algebra free, and neither completeness, nor infinite joins, nor a product
representation of the ring, nor a free presentation follows from the count of $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ branches. (4) The weak global and global dimensions
of the arithmetic fibre are open; the periodic resolution is exact only over the coefficient fibre, and no change-of-rings statement is made for the
arithmetic fibre or for $\Oz$. (5) The residue criterion is a finite algebraic criterion for represented algebraic Laurent elements, not a decision
procedure for arbitrary real coefficients or arbitrary surreal normal forms; substituting $T=0$ in a singular equation need not separate branches.
(6) The integer part of the Laurent field does not extend $\ct$ to the normalization; no single refinement removes all nilpotents; the ramification
filtration is not a valuation. (7) The finite checks ($18{,}040$ assertions in 12 categories, most of them clipped-order compositions and threshold
checks) count assertions, not theorems; they establish neither integral closure, nor the existence of finite places or prime extensions, nor
arbitrary-support summability, nor the normal-form embedding, nor cardinalities, nor exactness of an infinite resolution. (8) AI-assisted and
unrefereed; no Lean or other proof-assistant check, no repository build and no independent review; a compiled PDF is a document check. (9) Priority is
not certified: the literature comparison was targeted, and the repository comparison covered selected sections of this report, not all reports or
the history; nothing claims to settle a named factorization conjecture, uniqueness of surreal factorization, a global surcomplex analytic calculus
or the general theory of surreal supports. (10) Integral dependence, normalization of curves, valuation domains, quadratic square classes and periodic
resolutions are classical; the residue criterion is a proved pullback-style tool, not a claim to have invented pullback normalization; the
period-two mechanism has antecedents in matrix factorizations; the Newton--Puiseux theorem, the lifting of idempotents across nil ideals and the
uniqueness of the countable atomless Boolean algebra are classical and not claimed. (11) No continuum hypothesis and no regularity of $2^{\aleph_0}$
are used; all objects are sets, with ordinary choice and no class Zorn lemma, class module category or measurable cardinal; the repository's
descent theorem is compared, not used, and no unrefereed repository theorem is an input. (12) The questions concern precisely specified rings and do
not assert that the cyclic calculation settles an unrestricted Hahn problem; divisibility of the exponent group alone is not a proof of radicality.
(13) The formalization plan claims no implemented declaration and no repository build.

\paragraph{24.} (1) AI-assisted, unrefereed research draft with written proofs; no Lean or other proof-assistant check and no Wolfram computation;
historical priority is not certified; the generic equivalence of global choice with the class maximal-ideal principle may be familiar folklore, and the
monomial and support-prime statements may have antecedents in the generalized-series or ordered-monoid literature. (2) \Cref{osq:cr:thm:equivalence}
gives no lower bound for $\Oz$ itself: it does not show that a nonarithmetic maximal ideal of $\Oz$, or one above every $1+\omega^a$, implies global
choice; its converse uses arbitrary specially built class rings, and the maximal-ideal theorem for set rings yields only choice for sets. (3) The class
recursion is a class definition, not an effective algorithm; the finite-equation test quantifies over all ring elements and may be undecidable, and no
algorithm for ideal membership or decision procedure for membership in a chosen maximal ideal is given. (4) No canonical or choice-free maximal ideal is
constructed; uniformity is relative to a chosen global well-order, not parameter-free canonicity. (5) The continuum branching is a lower bound within one
fibre, not a spectrum: not every maximal ideal of the fibre is indexed by a branch, and $\Qa^k_a$ is not claimed to be a ring of functions on Cantor
space. (6) No cardinality is asserted for the collection of all class ideals and no class-sized Zariski space is formed; families of class ideals are
single class relations on parameters and ring elements. (7) Containing an algebraically closed class subfield does not make a residue field
algebraically closed; the residue fields are not claimed isomorphic to $\SC$, and their embeddings in $\SC$ need not be surjective. (8) The maps to
$\SC$ need not preserve order, strong summability, arbitrary infinite sums, exponentiation or any analytic structure; no analytic extension of complex
functions to all surcomplex arguments is claimed, and the algebraic closedness of $\SC$ is background, not reproved. (9) ``Residually surcomplex'' means
a separating family of homomorphisms: not residual finiteness, not a representation in a set-indexed product, not a single injective homomorphism with
maximal kernel; no product indexed by a proper class of class fields is used. (10) \Cref{osq:cr:thm:termprimes} needs both term-closure and strong
sum-closure; it is not a classification of all prime ideals and does not say that every omnific prime is a monomial prime. (11) No factorization
conjecture is used or addressed (refinement, unique factorization of generalized series); the existence and cutoff theorems classify neither all prime
ideals, nor all maximal ideals of a binomial fibre, nor all residue-field extensions of the embedded Hahn core. (12) The finite checks
($133{,}770$ assertions in six groups: greedy ideals in $\Z/n\Z$ and in products of $\F_2$, finite geometric remainders, dyadic algebra over $\F_{257}$,
finite branch filters, lexicographic scale examples) certify no class recursion, infinite Hahn sum, arbitrary surreal support, global choice or priority.
(13) The field cores, the dyadic product algebras and the Cantor-type subalgebra are this report's (07's), reproved and credited, not claimed; the greedy
Krull method, the compatibility mechanism of Hodges, Ern\'e and Entin (checked through Entin's corrected version, not against every line of Ern\'e's paper
or Hodges's), the characteristic-zero Hahn closure (Mac~Lane through Knight--Lange, Mac~Lane's paper not fully inspected), the rescaling automorphism, the
universality and back-and-forth method and $\Jac(A)=0$ are credited or called elementary; Conway and Gonshor are cited as standard, not reread. (14) Only
the comparison with set-sized targets uses the unrefereed universal theorem; the constructions and separation proofs do not. (15) The rescaling
\cref{osq:cr:prop:rescale} shows that the cutoff is an invariant of the embedded fibre at a chosen scale, not that the abstract fibres are
nonisomorphic, and the ordinal family changes the scale, so it gives no larger same-fibre count. (16) The repository comparison covered the pinned
report and selected guides, not every report or unintegrated companion, and absence from the excerpts was not taken as absence; the literature search
was targeted; the delivered Wikipedia link served for orientation only. (17) The eleven hypotheses 24's audit calls critical are kept: $\mathsf{GB}$ has
no choice and the unrestricted principle is not the restricted omnific one; ring elements are sets and cosets are coded by least representatives or Scott
codes; a stage stores a set of generators or a set partial embedding, never a proper-class ideal; ideal membership and rejection witnesses are finite
sums; every Hahn series has a set support and the geometric cancellation rests on summability, not convergence; $b>na$ must hold for \emph{every}
ordinary $n$; closure over a class exponent group is reduced polynomial by polynomial to set groups; a field core is not algebraic closedness; the
support-prime classification assumes both closure properties; the maps to $\SC$ need not preserve order, summability, infinite sums, exponentiation or
analytic structure; uniform families are relations, and no class of all class ideals and no proper-class-indexed product is formed. (18) Its audit's
record of what was not performed is kept: the proofs had internal review only, not independent peer review; the finite checks ran under Python~3.13.5;
no Lean, proof-assistant or Wolfram verification was performed; the PDF was built with pdfLaTeX and inspected visually. (19) The eight plausible but
incorrect arguments of 24's Section~11.2 are printed at the end of \cref{osq:cr:sub:residues}. (20) Its questions are not claimed resolved.

\paragraph{25.} (1) AI-assisted and unrefereed, with complete written arguments; no Lean formalization or build, no Wolfram computation and no
independent proof review; novelty is proposed relative to the inspected sources, priority is not certified, and no named longstanding conjecture
(factorization, birthdays, surreal exponentiation) is claimed settled. (2) The repository was read selectively through a connector whose long responses
were sometimes truncated, not checked out or built; newly delivered and unintegrated manuscripts were not exhaustively audited, an empty search was not
taken as evidence of absence, and it is not asserted that no equivalent statement occurs in them or in the wider literature. (3) The finite-difference
strategy, real polynomial rigidity, finite-order detection of smoothness and the nonflatness of tame functions are classical (Jones--Thomas--Wilkie,
Bhardwaj--McCulloch--Ramachandran--Woo, Miller, Bochnak--Coste--Roy) and not claimed; the Bhardwaj et al.\ preprint is cited in its inspected version
v1, without transferring its numerical growth constants; Miller's paper is a bibliographic and contextual antecedent, with limited full-text access, whose
specific argument is reproved; the Bochnak--Coste--Roy monograph was not reread in full. (4) The bound $\mathsf D^2$ is sufficient, not claimed optimal,
and concerns scalar graph descriptions; a degree bound for a full vector graph must first be converted by output elimination. (5) The graph degree is
that of a quantifier-free description; a bound for formulas with unresolved quantifiers is a different notion. (6) The mean-value and Rolle theorems are
used only for semialgebraic functions at finite order; nothing is asserted about unconstrained surreal-valued calculus. (7) The numerical-polynomial
normal form is exact algebra, not an algorithm on symbolic descriptions: equality, support membership and exact coefficient operations are not assumed
decidable; the Newton basis and the decompositions are inherited from this report. (8) $\ct$ is multiplicative only on nonnegative supports, not on
$\No$. (9) The bounded-window theorem asserts no regularity at the boundary of the box and supplies no holomorphic cutoff. (10) The shears are maps of the
lattice as a set, not ring automorphisms; the Jacobian statement is a triangular calculation, not a claim about the Jacobian conjecture; the surcomplex
shears are not holomorphic in general. (11) The surcomplex results are real-algebraic; no global surreal exponential or sine and no topology in which all
real analytic series converge is presupposed. (12) The Gaussian split is not a Gaussian binomial-basis theorem; ordinary binomial polynomials need not be
$\Z[i]$-valued. (13) The rank-one obstruction concerns the uniform monomial multiplier only, not the classification of semialgebraic preservers in rank
one; nonmonomial multipliers and restricted input domains need separate analysis. (14) $K_{\operatorname{cvx}(\Z a)}$ is used pointwise, through
set-sized divisible hulls; no union of supports over a proper class, no class Zorn lemma, no set of all class ideals and no class-indexed product is
used, and ``bounded'' in the two-end quotient is order-theoretic, with no compactness. (15) Nothing is classified for arbitrary class functions, all
finite-smoothness preservers, arbitrary omnific ideals, all polynomial automorphisms in several variables or holomorphic functions in an unrestricted
surreal calculus; no physical prediction is made. (16) The no-set-test theorem excludes coefficient-independent tests only, not coefficient-adapted
certificates or algorithms; it is a proper-class quantifier phenomenon, not a running-time statement. (17) The finite checks ($1{,}578$ exact assertions in
18 groups) verify finite identities, finite binomial jets, finite Newton grids and sampled lexicographic comparisons, not infinite supports, class
quantifiers, general semialgebraic calculus, the complete theorems or novelty; the PDF build is a document check, and the PowerShell build script was not
executed. (18) Some ingredients are elementary consequences of classical real algebraic geometry; independent review may find stronger antecedents, a
shorter formulation or errors. (19) The integer-part formula of $\Oz$ needs the correction for a negative infinitesimal remainder, and no argument drops it.

\paragraph{26.} (1) AI-assisted and proof-bearing, not refereed and not checked in Lean or by a machine; the arbitrary-cone formula and the detector
construction are proposed as original, but the searches did not establish priority, and no named general conjecture about $\No$ is claimed solved. (2)
$\pd(A_{\mathscr C}/\mathfrak r_{\mathcal F})=h+1$ is not claimed for $h\ge2$; only the interval $\max\{2,h\}\le\pd\le h+1$ is proved, and 21's exact orthant value is
credited, not used (for simplicial cones see the merge's isomorphism with $A_d$). (3) No all-module weak or global dimension of $A_{\mathscr C}$, $\Oz$ or $\GOz$
is asserted. (4) No extension to unrestricted infinite Hahn supports is asserted; every element has finite support. (5) The face-lattice reconstruction
needs the marked monomial grading; an unmarked recognition theorem is not claimed. (6) ``Core'' does not mean integer part of the fraction field, and a
partial exponent cone must not be replaced by the positive cone of the ambient order. (7) The numbers $\beta_{p,G}$ count summands of a reduced flat
resolution, not minimal free ranks, and the reduced resolution is not unique. (8) The geometric monomial class excludes arithmetic ideals such as
$pA_{\mathscr C}$ and restrictions on admitted coefficients. (9) Miller's real-polyhedral theory \cite{MillerEssential} is not identified with these
resolutions, and Geist--Miller's all-module theorems \cite{GeistMiller} are neither reproved nor claimed; cellular and lcm-lattice methods
\cite{BayerSturmfels,GPW} are classical. (10) \Cref{osq:pc:thm:arithmetic} concerns modules acting through $\ct$ only, not all modules over a core or the
class ring; the scalar-quotient calculation and the common fraction field are elementary comparisons, not new theorems. (11) The nonflatness concerns the
displayed two-ray relation for $d\ge2$; it does not deny the embeddings, the fraction field or the retraction, and asserts nothing about embeddings of
one-dimensional cores. (12) The homological-epimorphism theorem makes no recollement or compact-generation claim. (13) The finite checks
($52{,}080$ exact assertions, among them $188$ face quotients, $1{,}329$ further antichains, $56$ cancelled pairs and $2{,}457$ cap checks, with a fixed seed and
no exhaustive search) do not verify filtered colimits, exactness in every rational degree, the dual-basis argument, the topological contraction for every
polytope or normal forms, and are not an independent proof or referee report. (14) The repository was compared selectively (this report's lines 1--210 and
3300--3520 at the pin, its README, the root and catalogue READMEs and an automorphism-report README), not all reports or companion manuscripts, and an empty
connector search was not taken as absence. (15) All homological statements concern set-sized rings and modules; the full omnific ring appears only as the
target of an embedding and of a finite relation.

\paragraph{27.} (1) An author-side, internally reviewed, unrefereed draft with no Lean verification; historical priority is provisional, and no Riemann
hypothesis, omnific factorization conjecture or published automorphism problem is claimed solved. (2) No henselization or spectrum of the proper-class ring
$\Oz$ is asserted; all rings, spectra and henselizations are set-sized. (3) $\Idem(\mathscr G)$ and $\mathsf X$ are not classified: atomlessness, isolated
points and, for $\kappa=\aleph_0$, the Cantor space are open, and ``maximal'' is a cardinal statement only. (4) $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}$ and
$\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}[i]$ are local, not products of branches; nontrivial idempotents exist only in the generic fibre. (5) The imaginary unit lives only in
$\mathscr G$; $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}$ has no square root of $-1$ and residue field $\Q$. (6) The support projection is not a ring map, and the specializations
are maps of finite algebras, not evaluations of Laurent series at zero. (7) The rings are not Noetherian and no Krull dimension is determined; no
infinitesimal smoothness criterion applies. (8) The Gaussian decomposition does not assert $\mathsf X\not\cong\mathsf X\sqcup\mathsf X$. (9) The valuation
count imports de Felipe--Teissier \cite{DFT}; nothing is claimed about the components themselves or their topology compared with $\mathsf X$. (10) The finite
\'etale equivalence concerns $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}$, not $B_{\mathbb E}$ or $\Oz$, and the rank classification over $\mathscr G$ is of isomorphism classes,
not morphisms. (11) Only $K_0(\mathscr G)$ and finite projectives are computed; no higher $K$-theory or derived formula is asserted. (12) No birthday bound
is asserted; seeds are contained in $\mathbb E$, but the operations of a prior workspace are not preserved without further closure. (13) The finite checks
($5{,}760$ exact SymPy assertions, $5{,}586$ of them Boolean atoms; the count is not a measure of proof strength) prove no support, localization-denominator,
prime-existence, transfinite, cardinality or priority statement. (14) Henselian algebra, Boolean powers and the Stacks Project results are standard, de
Felipe--Teissier's theorem is imported, and the splitter mechanism is the repository's (20), re-derived. (15) Independent checking of the whole proof, in
particular of the bridge from supports to localization, is warranted; the exact Stone space, atomlessness, enlargement of the hull, mixed-characteristic
analogues and class-level geometry are not settled. (16) The repository changed during 27's inspection, so its guide reads are not a complete same-commit
audit; its search for ``hensel'' was not exhaustive (and missed existing occurrences, \cref{osq:hb:sub:henselian}); its targeted literature searches found no
primary source for the construction, which does not certify novelty. (17) No regularity of $\kappa$, continuum hypothesis, GCH or large cardinal is used.
(18) Its twelve questions are proposed directions and may already be answered in literature 27 did not locate.

\paragraph{The merge.} (1) The results marked \merge\ are consequences of the sources' lemmas; they
are no more refereed than the sources and are not formalized. (2) No general law is asserted for the
generator counts. (3) For full-support Hahn rings over a prescribed set group, exact thresholds are computed only in
\cref{osq:ex:lexQQ,osq:ex:countablecoeff}; the general questions of 04 and 10 stay open. (4) The
support-threshold theorem is stated for $k\in\{\R,\C\}$ as in 04 and 11, not for every set field.
(5) No Gaussian analogue of 10's congruence-preservation criterion is given. (6) Nothing is claimed about the
homological dimensions of the class ring $\Oz$; the weak global dimensions of the cores remain undetermined ($\pd_{A_d}D$ for
$d\ge2$, undetermined before the fifth batch, is $d+1$ by 21's \cref{osq:da:cor:exactpd}). (7) The finite-support cores of 12 and 14 are outside \cref{osq:thm:universal}: they have set-sized images
detecting the tail. (8) \Cref{osq:hd:prop:pd}(v) needs a countably generated tail; among the five constructions it settles
only $A^{08}_\kappa$ with $\cf\kappa=\aleph_0$. (9) The extensions of 17's results to $\kappa=\aleph_0$ and of its $\Tor$ formula to the cores
say nothing about the class ring's homological dimensions, and $R^{11}_{\aleph_0}$, like the cores, is outside \cref{osq:thm:universal}.
(10) The comparison of Gaussian tests concerns the sizes of two explicit certificates, not the minimal size of a test, and
\cref{osq:nf:rem:candidates} by itself decides nothing about $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$ (its candidates are decided in \cref{osq:bb:prop:candidates}).
(11) \Cref{osq:bb:cor:descent03} is a descent, not a membership test for $\NN_\kappa$, and \cref{osq:bb:prop:candidates} decides the idempotents
$(1+\bar u_H)/2$ only for $H=\iota_b(h)$ with $h\in TK_G[T]$, in particular for positive $H\in\Pi$ supported in one cyclic group; other $H$ are
not decided. (12) \Cref{osq:bb:rem:choice} concerns the splitting results only; the extension of branch maps and 19's detection still use global
choice. (13) The extension of 21's lattice theorem to every unital $D$ (\cref{osq:da:thm:lattice}) and \cref{osq:da:rem:htwo} give no projective
dimension for the five constructions or for $R^{11}_\kappa$ with uncountable $\kappa$; the remark shows only that (H2) cannot be dropped from
\cref{osq:hd:prop:pd}(v). (14) The comparison of 22's and 16's rational certificates (\cref{osq:ft:rem:probes}) concerns the sizes of two explicit
certificates, not the least size of a test. (15) \Cref{osq:ft:rem:otherD} says nothing for $D=k$, and the remark after \cref{osq:ft:prop:relative}
decides nothing about finite certificates in a workspace without fresh exponents. (16) The comparisons of \cref{osq:rm:rem:fullclass,osq:rm:ex:sqrt}
concern the real pair; \cref{osq:rm:rem:puiabstract} concerns the bounded-denominator Puiseux ring only and determines neither the isomorphism type
nor the order density of its Boolean algebra; \cref{osq:rm:rem:booleanform} rests on applying the proof of \cref{osq:bb:prop:fixedboolean}
verbatim to the coefficient field $\overline\Q\cap\R$, and nothing is claimed for noncyclic groups or for the Hahn field over $\Q a$.
(17) The eighth-batch merge results need 24's foundation where they use maximal ideals: the extension of point evaluations in
\cref{osq:cr:rem:evaluation} uses global choice, is not canonical and does not land in $\EE_a$; \cref{osq:cr:rem:ultrafilters} gives class
ultrafilters in $\mathsf{GBC}$ only; and the copy of $\SC$ in \cref{osq:cr:cor:properfield} makes the residue fields neither algebraically closed nor
isomorphic to $\SC$. (18) \Cref{osq:sa:rem:threshold} concerns monomial multipliers and the real pair; \cref{osq:sa:rem:exceptionsnecessary} shows only
that global smoothness cannot be weakened to $C^{\mathsf k}$ in \cref{osq:sa:cor:exceptions}, not what the exceptional sets of finitely smooth maps are;
and the batch-34 status of \cref{osq:ft:q:maps} re-scopes 22's comment, it does not supply a piecewise classification.
(19) The isomorphism of a rational simplicial cone core with $A_d$ transfers 21's exact projective dimensions to simplicial face quotients only; for
nonsimplicial quotients with $h\ge2$ the endpoint stays open, and \cref{osq:pc:rem:lattice} gives a lower bound for the weak global dimension, not its
value. (20) The identification of 27's $\sqrt{\Pi\NN}$ with $\Pi\NN$ uses 19's \cref{osq:nf:thm:radical}, which 27 neither uses nor needs, and the branch
counts compared in \cref{osq:hb:rem:counts} concern three different rings; nothing is inferred about $\Oz$ itself.

\subsection{Open questions and their status}\label{osq:sub:questions}
The sources pose the following questions, each as a question suggested by the proofs rather than as
an established open problem. Several coincide and are merged.

\begin{question}[Least detecting targets over a fixed exponent group; 03, 04, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 13, 15]\label{osq:q:fixed}
For a set-sized ordered group $\Gamma$, a family of admissible supports and a specified element (or
the whole positive-support ideal), what is the least cardinality of a ring target detecting it, and
which intrinsic support conditions characterize it?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open in general. The field bound (\cref{osq:prop:fieldbound}) is a lower bound that is
exact for the five constructions and for the two examples of \cref{osq:sub:fieldbound}; there it answers
04's ``optimal small targets'' question for its own example, and for 10's question ``when is the
bound attained'' it shows that the bound need not be attained (in the rational example, and for
$A^{03}_{\aleph_1}$ if CH fails). 08's criterion
and 11's coinitiality theorem give sufficient conditions (07's ``sharp set-sized analogues'' and 09's
``quantitative problem'' are the same question). 13's question (how large a target must be to detect a prescribed
series, and whether its divisibility bound is optimal) and 15's ``optimal local cardinal bounds'' are this question as
well: their bounds are the monomial count of \cref{osq:prop:monomialbounds}(ii), which the field bound dominates; the
threshold theorem (\cref{osq:thm:thresholds}) answers them for the five constructions, and \cref{osq:ex:countablecoeff}
shows that the monomial bound need not be attained.

\begin{question}[Cardinal arithmetic without the matching hypothesis; 06]\label{osq:q:kappa}
For $\kappa$ uncountable regular with $\kappa^{<\kappa}>\kappa$, what is the least size of a target
detecting a nonzero element of $\Pi^{06}_\kappa$, and is there an integer part of size exactly $\kappa$
with the same lower bound?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Answered. The least size is $\kappa^{<\kappa}$ in ZFC (\cref{osq:thm:model06}, a merge
result from 06's collision lemma); 08 constructs, for every infinite $\kappa$ in ZFC, an integer part of
size exactly $\kappa$ with threshold $\kappa$ (\cref{osq:thm:model08}), without claiming its fraction field.

\begin{question}[Higher projective dimension; 06]\label{osq:q:pd}
What is $\pd_A\Z$ for the set-sized integer parts, and how does it depend on the cofinality of the
principal-ideal chain?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Partly answered. $\fd_AD=1$ and $\pd_AD\ge2$ are known for all five constructions. If the tail is
countably generated, that is if the principal-ideal chain has countable cofinality, then $\pd_AD=2$
(\cref{osq:hd:prop:pd}(v), a merge result from 12's telescope); among the five constructions this is the case exactly for
$A^{08}_\kappa$ with $\cf\kappa=\aleph_0$. For chains of uncountable cofinality (03, 06, 09, 11, and 08 with
$\cf\kappa>\aleph_0$) the question stays open. For comparison, the ordered-cone cores have $\pd D=2$ and the
coordinate-cone cores $\pd_{A_d}D=d+1$ (21, \cref{osq:da:cor:exactpd}), although their tails are countably generated: they fail (H2)
(\cref{osq:da:rem:htwo}); 17's countable lexicographic model has $\pd D=2$ and
$\pd L(M)=2$ (\cref{osq:rel:rem:alephzero}), and 17 asks the same question for its uncountable models (\cref{osq:rel:q:relations}).

\begin{question}[Nonarithmetic primes and their residue fields; 06, 07]\label{osq:q:primes}
Which prime or maximal class ideals of $\Oz$ have nonzero constant-term image and zero intersection with
$\Z$, and which class fields occur as $\Frac(\Oz/P)$ for primes $P\not\supseteq\Pi$? Can the embedded
field $\FF_a$ distinguish such primes?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. Necessary conditions: \cref{osq:if:cor:primefield,osq:if:prop:reservoir,osq:if:rem:composition}.
\emph{Status (batch 34).} Partly answered, with global choice. The existence clause is answered by 24: every maximal class ideal containing
$1+\omega^a$, or any nonconstant element with unit constant term, is a nonarithmetic prime with $P\cap\Z=0$ and $P\not\subseteq\Pi$, and such ideals exist
in $\mathsf{GBC}$ (\cref{osq:cr:thm:binomialmax,osq:cr:cor:unitconstant,osq:cr:prop:arithmetic}); they separate the points of $\Oz$
(\cref{osq:cr:thm:separation}), and there are at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ of them above each $1+\omega^a$ and a family indexed by $\On\times\Z_2$ across scales
(\cref{osq:cr:thm:cantor,osq:cr:thm:twoaxes}). On the second clause: every maximal residue field of characteristic $0$ embeds in $\SC$
(\cref{osq:cr:thm:residually}) and, above $1+\omega^a$, contains a copy of $\SC$ (\cref{osq:cr:cor:properfield}); which fields occur is not determined
(\cref{osq:cr:q:closed,osq:cr:q:relative}). On the third: the embedded $\FF_a$ meets every maximal ideal above $1+\omega^a$ trivially, a field mapping injectively to every
nonzero quotient, so by itself it does not distinguish them; the maximal ideals of \cref{osq:cr:thm:cantor} are separated by the dyadic idempotents over
$\EE_a$, and the monomial cutoff \cref{osq:cr:thm:cutoff} separates the scales \merge. The classification of nonarithmetic primes stays open, as does existence without global choice (\cref{osq:cr:q:choice,osq:cr:q:definable}).
The primes that are term-closed and strongly sum-closed are classified, and none of characteristic $0$ is maximal (\cref{osq:cr:thm:termprimes}).

\begin{question}[The ambient binomial quotient; 07]\label{osq:q:binomial}
Which normal-form invariants describe the elements and ideals of $\Qa_a$ beyond the Cantor algebra;
which idempotents lie outside it; how are cyclotomic decompositions at different scales related?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. \emph{Status (batch 34).} Partly addressed by 24. Every monomial $\omega^b$, $b\ge0$, is zero or a unit in $\Qa_a$, zero exactly
when $a\ll b$ (\cref{osq:cr:thm:cutoff}); the whole tail above $\operatorname{cvx}(\Z a)$ can be discarded, $\Qa_a$ being the binomial quotient of the
elements supported in $\operatorname{cvx}(\Z a)$ (\cref{osq:cr:prop:tails}); the binomial quotients at separated scales are comaximal, and those at
different scales are abstractly isomorphic by rescaling (\cref{osq:cr:cor:comaximal,osq:cr:prop:rescale}), which relates the cyclotomic decompositions
at different scales; and every branch of the Cantor algebra lies in a maximal ideal (\cref{osq:cr:thm:cantor}). Idempotents outside the Cantor algebra,
the nilradical and the prime ideals of $\Qa_a$ remain open. 24 asks the same question in sharper form (its Question~12.6): determine the nilradical and
the Jacobson radical of $\Qa^k_a$; is $(1+\omega^a)$ radical; how much of the idempotent algebra is generated by finite rational-exponent blocks; and what
information beyond the monomial cutoff and the dyadic branch data determines a maximal ideal? 24's comments: the reduction to
$\operatorname{cvx}(\Z a)$ should be used first, but it still leaves a proper-class infinitesimal exponent core and general infinite supports, and finite
polynomial squarefreeness does not by itself give radicality in the full non-Noetherian Hahn support ring.

\begin{question}[Residue fields of the set-sized models; 08, 09]\label{osq:q:residue}
Which characteristic-zero fields of the threshold cardinality occur as maximal residue fields of
$A^{08}_\kappa$ and of $A^{09}_{\lambda,D}$, and how many maximal ideals are there?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open; existence, cardinality and at least $\lambda$ nonarithmetic maximal ideals
(for 09) are proved.

\begin{question}[Extra structure on the workspace; 08]\label{osq:q:extra}
Can prescribed residue-field behaviour be combined with closure under a surreal derivation or an
exponential, or with an initial embedding, without destroying the finite-coordinate invariant or the
cardinality?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open.

\begin{question}[Intermediate rings; 04, 11, 15]\label{osq:q:intermediate}
Which rings between the finite-support ring and $D+\Pi_k$ (for instance, given by allowed families of
support order types) still have set-sized reflection $D$? Is enough closure under subordinate division
also necessary?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open; \cref{osq:thm:support} settles the case of cardinal support bounds. 09's question on
support bounds below a regular cardinal is addressed for the groups of 06 and 11
(\cref{osq:sub:model06,osq:sub:model11}), where the support sizes of inverses and quotients are checked.

\begin{question}[Beyond ring observations; 04]\label{osq:q:weaker}
Which weaker multiplicative compatibility conditions still force factorization through the residue, and
which structured families of set-sized local models can retain a specified family of scales?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open.

\begin{question}[Invisible class domains and automorphisms; 10, 11, 15]\label{osq:q:invisible}
What are the ideals, class-valued representations and factorization theory of proper-class quotient
domains invisible to all set-sized rings? How much can an automorphism of $\Oz$ do inside $\Pi$ while
fixing $\ct$?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Partly answered (batch 31). The first sentence is open. The second is answered in the report on
omnific-preserving automorphisms \cite{RepoOpa} (\nolinkurl{opa:as:cor:invisible}, from its automatic-strongness
theorem \nolinkurl{opa:as:thm:main} and its factorization \nolinkurl{opa:as:thm:factor}, proved by that report's sources
12 and 13 and independently by its source 14). Every ring automorphism $\sigma$ of $\Oz$ satisfies $\ct\circ\sigma=\ct$,
and extends uniquely to a strong automorphism of $\No$ fixing $\R$ pointwise, of the form $M_{\chi,\tau}\circ u$.
Here $\tau$ is an order automorphism of the exponents, $\chi$ a positive character and $u$ a strong leading-term-fixing
automorphism preserving $\Oz$, classified by that report's convex-support criterion \nolinkurl{opa:thm:criterion}. On
$\Pi$ it therefore acts first by $u$, then by an exponent automorphism and a positive rescaling of monomials; every such
composition occurs.

\begin{question}[Normalization; 03]\label{osq:q:normalization}
Give a membership test for $\NN$ on mixed supports; describe the integral closure over a fixed finitely
generated exponent subgroup; decide the descent $\NN\cap F^{03}_\kappa=\NN_\kappa$; find the algebra
generation number of $\NN_\kappa$ between $\cf\kappa$ and $\kappa^{\aleph_0}$; find a class-sized
replacement for the valuative criterion of integrality; describe the infinite set-sized images of $\NN$.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Partly answered. For the last clause, 19 classifies the set-sized \emph{domain} images of $\NN$ and $\NN_\C$ (they are
$\overline\Z$ and $\Fpbar$, \cref{osq:nf:thm:domainimages}) and shows that every set-sized image factors through
$\NN/\Pi\NN\cong\overline\Z[\Idem]$ (\cref{osq:nf:cor:small,osq:nf:thm:boolean}); images with zero divisors are not classified. 20 shows that
$\Idem(\NN/\Pi\NN)$ is atomless and a proper class and that no set-indexed family of set-sized images is jointly faithful
(\cref{osq:bb:thm:atoms,osq:bb:thm:noseparating}); its isomorphism type is open (\cref{osq:bb:q:structure}). The descent clause is answered
affirmatively: $\NN\cap F^{03}_\kappa=\NN_\kappa$ (\cref{osq:bb:cor:descent03}, a merge result from 20's support projection). The clause on a
fixed exponent subgroup is partly answered: for every set-sized subgroup $G$, $\NN\cap K_G$ is the integral closure $\NN(G)$ of the omnific
integers supported in $G$, so integrality witnesses at larger scales never help, and for $G=\Z a$ the rational one-scale slice is determined
exactly (\cref{osq:bb:thm:descent,osq:bb:thm:rational}); a description of $\NN(G)$ in general is open. \emph{Status (batch 32).} For $G=\Z a$ the
clause is answered by 23: $\NN(\Z a)$ is the set of elements of $K_{\Z a}$ integral over $\R[\omega^a]$ whose residues at the finitely many places over
$\omega^a=0$ of each finite subextension are algebraic integers, and its $\R$-linear span is the integral closure of $\R[\omega^a]$
(\cref{osq:rm:thm:residues,osq:rm:thm:span}; the same holds for the Gaussian pair with $\C$ in place of $\R$). This is a criterion, not an algorithm (\cref{osq:nf:q:fibre}(c)), and for
noncyclic finitely generated $G$ a description stays open. The membership test, the generation
number and the valuative criterion stay open; 19 asks the same membership question, for supports in one finitely generated
exponent subgroup first, allowing integrality witnesses at larger scales, and 20 asks for effective support-local certificates
(\cref{osq:nf:q:fibre}(c)). 04's question on Diophantine fibers belongs to the sibling report
\cite{RepoOdg}, and so does 13's question on fibers of polynomials with nonlinear factors.

\begin{question}[Homological dimensions of the cores; 12, 14, 21, merge]\label{osq:hd:q:cores}
For $d\ge2$, is $\pd_{A_d}D$ equal to $d$ or to $d+1$? When $K\ne\Frac D$, what are the weak global dimensions of $A_d$ (at least $d+1$) and of
$A_0=A_1$ (at least $2$)? How do cores over non-simplicial cones, their arbitrary ideals and their homological
localizations behave?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Partly answered. The first clause is answered by 21: $\pd_{A_d}D=d+1$ for every $d\ge1$ (\cref{osq:da:cor:exactpd}); in rank
one this is the merge value $2$ of \cref{osq:hd:prop:pd}, and over every ordered-cone core $\pd D=2$. The weak global dimensions stay open,
when $K\ne\Frac D$, with lower bounds $d+1$ and $2$ (\cref{osq:hd:sub:dimensions}); for $D=K$ the rank-one weak global dimension is $1$, as shown after \cref{osq:da:thm:lattice}. 21 adds $\operatorname{gl.dim}A_d\ge d+2$ when $K\ne\Frac D$
(\cref{osq:da:thm:lattice}) and asks whether the bounds $\operatorname{gl.dim}A_d\ge d+2$ and $\operatorname{w.gl.dim}A_d\ge d+1$ are sharp,
which is merged here. Cores over non-simplicial cones, arbitrary ideals and homological localizations stay open.

\emph{Status (batch 34).} The non-simplicial clause is answered by 26 for flat dimension, for the quotients by radical coefficient-full monomial ideals:
over the core $A_{\mathscr C}$ of any pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone, $\fd(A_{\mathscr C}/\mathfrak r_{\mathcal F})$ is the top degree of the
reduced homology of finite join complexes, with explicit cap-module witnesses (\cref{osq:pc:thm:exactfd}); the quotient keeping a face $F$ has flat
dimension the largest dimension of a face disjoint from $F$ (\cref{osq:pc:thm:facebetti}), so $\fd D=d$ for every cone, the cone is simplicial exactly when
all facet quotients have flat dimension one (\cref{osq:pc:thm:simplicial}), and cube cones have facet quotients of flat dimension $d-1$
(\cref{osq:pc:thm:cubes}). Projective dimensions are bracketed, $\max\{2,h\}\le\pd\le h+1$ (\cref{osq:pc:cor:pdbounds}), and for simplicial cones the upper
endpoint holds, a simplicial core being $A_d$ (21's \cref{osq:da:cor:exactpd}; merge). 26 asks the same two questions (its Questions~13.1, 13.2),
merged here: for a radical geometric quotient with $h=\fd\ge2$, when is $\pd=h+1$ and can it equal $h$; is the upper endpoint universal for rational
cones and arbitrary $D\subseteq K$; and what are $\operatorname{w.gl.dim}A_{\mathscr C}$ and $\operatorname{gl.dim}A_{\mathscr C}$ for nonsimplicial
cones, with explicit hypotheses on $D$ and $K$? 26's comments: a plausible step is to combine the cap detector with the non-splitting of a countable
telescope to build a nonzero $\Ext^{h+1}$ class, controlling compatibility across the face differential, which flat detection alone does not do; its
theorem gives $\operatorname{w.gl.dim}A_{\mathscr C}\ge d$, not an all-module upper bound; Geist--Miller's orthant theorems \cite{GeistMiller} address a
stronger all-module problem in their setting; and extending a total Koszul or diagonal resolution to a nonsimplicial arithmetic core differs from resolving
only the face quotients. The lower bound is already $d+1$ when $K\ne\Frac D$, by lattice modules (\cref{osq:pc:rem:lattice}, a merge remark). Arbitrary ideals,
homological localizations and the exact weak global and global dimensions stay open.

\begin{question}[Beyond one coefficient lattice; 14, 21]\label{osq:tn:q:lattices}
Replace the single coefficient lattice by a finite filtration of lattices indexed by support levels and determine which
extension data survive multiplication; characterize all finitely generated rank-one modules with double dual $B$; determine
how coefficient rings that are not principal ideal domains change the tensor kernel.
\end{question}
