\emph{Status.} Open. 21 asks the first part again, for the derived tensor products of finitely generated omnific ideals whose generators
lie at several independent boundary levels, and notes that its common-scale DGA (\cref{osq:da:thm:dga}) does not cover them; its question is
merged here.

\begin{question}[Fresh scales; 16]\label{osq:fs:q:fresh}
(a) Can the factorial-residue Gaussian certificate be replaced by an optimal or near-optimal grid, and how does a regular basis
of $\Int(\Z[i])$ interact with the omnific splitting? (b) Under what hypotheses are the formal inverse branches of a polynomial
map in several variables at independently fresh coordinates classified by finitely many forbidden support blocks (triangular
automorphisms exclude a direct analogue of one-variable surjectivity rigidity)? (c) For a fixed set-sized Hahn subfield and its
nonnegative-support ring, which coefficient subgroups admit enough dominant extensions inside the field to recover the image
gap and the rational certificates?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Partly answered. (a) is partly addressed by 18: its Gaussian simplex test is smaller than the factorial-residue certificate for
$d\ge3$, and every ordinary testing set for $\Int(\Z[i])$, for instance the Volkov--Petrov sets of size $O(d)$ in one variable, also tests
$\GOz$ (\cref{osq:or:prop:gausstest}); the optimal size is not determined. 22 reduces the constant-test part of (a) exactly to the ordinary
problem: a finite subset of $\Z[i]^m$ tests preservation of $\GOz$ in a coordinate degree space if and only if it tests $\Int(\Z[i]^m)$ there
(\cref{osq:ft:thm:lifting}); its question on sharp Gaussian constant tests (how far known ordinary Gaussian universal sets improve the surcomplex
certificate once combined with the remote denominator stage, distinguishing coordinate from total degree in several variables) is merged here, and
22 claims no optimality for its grid $C_{d+1}^{\,m}$. For (c), 18's discrete-gap arguments, unlike the fresh-scale
ones, do hold in fixed Hahn workspaces (\cref{osq:or:cor:workspace}); and 22 answers the part on rational certificates for its single-scale
certificates: a coefficient subgroup $G$ of the value group $\Gamma$ has a fresh exponent in $\Gamma$ exactly when the convex subgroup it generates is
proper, and then the Laurent blocks, the detector and the certificates hold in the workspace (\cref{osq:ft:prop:relative}). The image gap in a fixed
workspace, the corresponding condition for 16's multi-exponent probes (\cref{osq:fs:thm:probes}), and the existence of other finite certificates when
that convex subgroup is all of $\Gamma$ stay open, as does (b).

\begin{question}[Relations of lattice ideals; 17, 21]\label{osq:rel:q:relations}
(a) Classify the kernels of omnific matrices with several monomial scales, and determine which coefficient-lattice data beyond $q$ and
$\ell$ they need. (b) Determine the projective dimensions of $\Pi^{11}_\kappa$ and $J_g(M)$ over $R^{11}_\kappa$, and an upper bound for its weak
global dimension. (c) How much of a finitely generated coefficient algebra do the product lattices, $\Hom$ modules and mixed
multiplication kernels together reconstruct?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open, except (b) for $\kappa=\aleph_0$: $\pd\Pi^{11}_{\aleph_0}=1$ and $\pd J_g(M)=2$ for $r\ge2$ (\cref{osq:rel:rem:alephzero}, a merge
result). For uncountable $\kappa$, (b) is \cref{osq:q:pd} for $R^{11}_{\Gamma_\kappa,<\kappa}$; (a) is also 14's question (\cref{osq:tn:q:lattices}).
(c) is partly addressed by 21: with the distinguished $1$ and the boundary embedding, the self multiplication kernel
$\mathcal T(\mathfrak o,\mathfrak o)$ recovers the multiplication of an order (\cref{osq:da:thm:reconstruction}), and 17's
\cref{osq:rel:thm:order} recovers the order from $\End_A(J_\gamma(\mathfrak o))$; 21 asks which parts of these framed data can be recovered
intrinsically from a category of omnific quotient modules with its tensor structure, which is merged into (c).

\begin{question}[Ordinary-output loci; 18]\label{osq:or:q:outputs}
(a) Which hypotheses on $f\in\Num_n(\Lambda)$ exclude positive-dimensional fibres and make its ordinary-output locus a finite union of
translated ordinary lattices, explaining both the linewise rigidity and the example $XY$? (b) For a polynomial of degree $d$ without a rich
target, which patterns of the numbers $\#\mathcal L_{f,b}\in\{0,\dots,d\}$ occur as $b$ varies? (c) Can Gaussian test points in $\GOz$
that are not ordinary reduce the least number of test points below the ordinary minimum? (d) Can the cluster theorem be formalized for
an abstract discretely ordered ring and specialized through the normal-form bridge?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. The real analogue of (c) is settled by 16: for $\Oz^n$ no set of omnific points smaller than $|L|$ tests a
lower-set space $V_L$ (\cref{osq:fs:thm:lower}); for $\GOz$ the lower bound $d+1$ from the dimension is all that is known. 22's lifting theorem
(\cref{osq:ft:thm:lifting}) concerns test points in $\Z[i]^m$ only and does not bear on (c).

\begin{question}[The arithmetic fibre of the normalization; 19]\label{osq:nf:q:fibre}
(a) Determine $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$: is it trivial, does it have atoms, can independent families of nontrivial idempotents be constructed,
and is it a set? (b) For which fixed exponent groups and support classes is the extended ideal radical in the corresponding real
integral closure, and when does real-rooted lifting give a Boolean-power fibre although set-family divisibility fails? (c) Given finitely
many integral elements with monic witnesses, can a common Boolean partition and its algebraic-integer coefficients be extracted by a
concrete symbolic procedure, including the equality tests in the quotient?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Partly answered. (a) is answered by 20: $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$ is nontrivial and atomless, it is a proper class with no
set-sized order-dense subset, the explicit family of \cref{osq:bb:thm:ordinal} is independent and indexed by all ordinals, and free families of
every set size exist over every set-sized subring (\cref{osq:bb:thm:uniform,osq:bb:thm:free,osq:bb:thm:ordinal,osq:bb:thm:atoms}); the same holds for
$\mathsf B_\C$ (\cref{osq:bb:cor:complex}). The earlier reduction of (a) to instances of the membership clause of \cref{osq:q:normalization}
(\cref{osq:nf:rem:candidates}) is superseded: 20 needs no membership test, and the candidates of that remark are nontrivial
(\cref{osq:bb:prop:candidates}, a merge result). What remains of (a) is the isomorphism type (\cref{osq:bb:q:structure}). (b) is partly
answered: for every nonzero set-sized ordered group the reduced fibre $\mathsf C(G)$ is a Boolean power of $\overline\Z$, and one dominant
coordinate adds free Boolean families (\cref{osq:bb:prop:fixedboolean,osq:bb:thm:rank}); whether $\Pi(G)\NN(G)$ is radical, and whether
$\Idem(\mathsf C(G))$ is atomless, in a fixed workspace was left open by 20, which asks the same; for cyclic groups it is now decided (batch 32,
below). (c) is open; 20 asks it for algebraic Laurent
elements given by equations and branch data, with complexity bounds, and settles the one-scale rational case
(\cref{osq:bb:thm:rational}); 23 gives a criterion for cyclic groups (below). \Cref{osq:nf:thm:doubling} holds throughout. 19's membership question is
merged into \cref{osq:q:normalization}.

\emph{Status (batch 32).} (b) is decided for every nonzero cyclic group $G=\Z a$ by 23, in opposite directions: $\Pi(\Z a)\NN(\Z a)$ is not radical,
its fibre having nilpotents of every index (\cref{osq:rm:thm:explicit}), and $\Idem(\mathsf C(\Z a))$ is atomless of cardinality and order density
$2^{\aleph_0}$ (\cref{osq:rm:cor:atomless,osq:rm:thm:cardinality}), also for the Gaussian pair. For the bounded-denominator Puiseux support class over
$\Q a$ the extended ideal is radical (\cref{osq:rm:thm:pui}), and there real-rooted lifting gives a Boolean-power fibre although set-family divisibility
fails (\cref{osq:rm:rem:puiabstract}, a merge observation). For other groups and support classes (b) stays open, and the Hahn field over $\Q a$ is
\cref{osq:rm:q:fullQ}. 23 asks the same question (its Question~10.2): for a prescribed set-sized $G$, which properties of $G$ and of the admitted
supports determine radicality of $\Pi(G)\NN(G)$, and can the one-variable ramification filtration be replaced by a finite-rank or cut-valued
filtration when $G$ has several Archimedean layers? 23's comments: the cyclic negative and the Puiseux positive results are two test cases that any
criterion must distinguish; a next model is a lexicographic sum of two cyclic groups, where the coefficient block is a field with its own integer
part and the residue-basis step of \cref{osq:rm:thm:span} needs a replacement; the proof does not classify groups with a discrete convex component.
(c) is addressed for cyclic groups by 23's residue criterion (\cref{osq:rm:thm:residues,osq:rm:rem:effective}), which is a criterion and not an algorithm.
23 asks (its Question~10.7), for coefficients in a number field or a computable presentation of $\overline\Q$, for an algorithm that takes a finite
algebraic function field and a chosen Laurent branch at infinity, decides membership in $\NN(\Z a)$, computes $\nu_T(f)$, and produces a monic
certificate and the least refinement killing a nilpotent residue. 23's comments: the outputs are determined (normalize at the finite places, test
the residues, compute the finitely many orders), and what remains is a representation and complexity problem; singular plane equations can hide
branches, so normalization cannot in general be replaced by factoring one specialized polynomial; one would bound the certificate degree
$dr\deg Q$ of \cref{osq:rm:rem:effective} in the input degree and height and decide when smaller certificates exist.

\begin{question}[The class Boolean algebra of the fibre; 20]\label{osq:bb:q:structure}
Which further Boolean invariants determine $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$? Can its automorphisms, or its possible infinite joins, be characterized
directly in terms of support-local arithmetic?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. Known: it is atomless, a proper class with no set-sized order-dense subset, and relatively free over every set-sized
subring in every set size (\cref{osq:bb:thm:free,osq:bb:thm:atoms}); this does not make it free, complete or saturated.

\begin{question}[Finite certificates at new scales; 22]\label{osq:ft:q:certificates}
(a) What is the smallest coefficient-uniform remote test set for rational functions with given degree bounds and a prescribed fresh $t$; can the
bivariate count $5d^2+6d+3$ of \cref{osq:ft:thm:certificate} be improved with an explicit coefficient-independent choice of the ordinary coordinates?
(b) Can total-degree bounds, Newton polytopes or prescribed monomial supports replace the rectangular degree space and give substantially smaller
tests? (c) For which useful notations of surreal coefficients can a certified group bound and a symbolic fresh scale be produced effectively?
(d) Given sign-sequence descriptions of a support bound, what ordinal birthday bounds hold for the witness $t$ and for a bad input produced by the
resultant method? (e) Can sufficient fresh-scale conditions for a bounded-degree family be expressed without naming normal-form supports, for instance
in the pair $(\No,\Oz)$, possibly with predicates for convex subgroups? (f) Can the support-block and finite-certificate proofs be added as a small,
independently auditable extension of the repository's Hahn layer?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 22's comments: in (a) the proof ignores the structure of the resultant and uses one bound in every direction, and an optimality
claim must say whether the test set may depend on the coefficients or only on their support group and degrees; 16's probe certificate uses fewer values
with $m+1$ fresh exponents (\cref{osq:ft:rem:probes}). In (b) the dimension lower bound holds for any finite-dimensional polynomial space with a rich
input set, achieving it with integer-valued nodes is an arithmetic issue, and on the rational side sparse resultants must still exclude cancellation and
degree loss; lower-set spaces, including total degree, are already tested optimally (\cref{osq:fs:thm:lower}), and 16's probes give total-degree
rational certificates (\cref{osq:fs:cor:certificates}). In (c) a first implementation would use finite normal forms with exponents in a computable
ordered group and the fresh scale as an extra lexicographic generator, a second infinite supports with certified bounding data; coefficient equality,
support membership, support bounding and ring membership should be separate parts of the input contract, none following from the other three
(compare 16's non-claim (4) and \cref{osq:nf:q:fibre}(c)). In (d) the construction of the fresh exponent as $\omega$ times a bound proves existence
only; bounds should come from the representation used, with every multiplication and monomial operation accounted for. In (e) a merely
transcendental test point is not enough, since its order relative to the coefficient scales is essential, and the certificate is not quantifier
elimination for the pair. In (f) the milestones are the order embedding $(n,g)\mapsto nb+g$ on lexicographic blocks, reverse well-ordering and local
finiteness of the Laurent image, multiplicativity, the nonnegative-support detector, the resultant bound and the grid lemma, and the explicit deceptive
function, with the proper-class conclusions proved through an explicit small-set bounding interface; a finite-rank toy model would not establish the
full claims (\cref{osq:sub:formalization}).

\begin{question}[Arithmetic maps beyond affine polynomial space; 22]\label{osq:ft:q:maps}
(a) Which single-valued algebraic or semialgebraic maps preserve $\Oz$, and do their branches admit analogous certificates? (b) Which affine
varieties admit a counterpart of the constant-grid and remote-direction certificate for their omnific points? (c) How are the polynomial
automorphisms whose two directions preserve $\Oz^m$ organized by their ordinary specializations and purely infinite parts? (d) How far do the
finite certificates and the absence of set-sized tests extend to rings $D\oplus\Pi_k$ for other infinite subrings $D$ of $k$, for instance rings of
algebraic integers?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open, with (d) partly addressed. 22's comments: in (a) a global polynomial conclusion is false ($|X|$ preserves $\Oz$ and is only
piecewise polynomial), and the target is a piecewise classification with explicit branch hypotheses and finite complexity bounds, controlling algebraic
branches and their negative-support tails. In (b) the affine proof uses the Zariski density of an ordinary grid and free movement in one coordinate,
neither automatic on a variety; a first theorem could fix an explicit dominant parametrization and track its exceptional locus, and varieties with very
few ordinary integral points need a different mechanism. In (c) \cref{osq:ft:cor:birational} removes denominators but does not classify the group, which
the triangular binomial shears of \cref{osq:ft:ex:shear} show to be larger than the group with coefficients in $\Oz$; a start is the subgroup generated
by affine maps and triangular binomial shears, together with the kernel of specialization, and nothing is implied about all automorphisms in higher
dimension. This is not the question on automorphisms of the ring $\Oz$ in \cref{osq:q:invisible}. In (d) the detector is insensitive to $D$, the
polynomial step needs integer-valued polynomial theory over $D$, and the deceiver needs a constant outside $D$ with a suitable cleared denominator;
16 already proves rational collapse, the transfer $\Num_r(\A_{D,k})=\Int(D^r)\oplus\Pi_k[\mathbf X]$, the probe certificates and the one-variable
removal of exceptions for every unital $D\subseteq k$ (\cref{osq:fs:thm:collapse,osq:fs:prop:transfer,osq:fs:thm:probes,osq:fs:thm:cosmall}), and the
absence of set-sized tests holds for every $D\ne k$ (\cref{osq:ft:rem:otherD}, a merge result); finite constant test sets for $\Int(D^m)$ and the
lifting theorem for general $D$ remain open.

\emph{Status (batch 34).} The first clause of (a) is answered by 25 for globally smooth maps, in every dimension: a globally $C^\infty$ semialgebraic
map $\No^r\to\No^{r'}$ preserves $\Oz^r$ if and only if its coordinates are integer-valued polynomials, with explicit binomial expansions, and global
$C^{\mathsf D^2}$ regularity suffices at scalar graph degree $\mathsf D$ (\cref{osq:sa:thm:smoothmany,osq:sa:cor:explicit}); the same holds over every real
closed field with a cofinal discretely ordered subring, and for $\GOz$ in real coordinates (\cref{osq:sa:thm:complexreal}). A semialgebraic preserver of $\Oz$
whose graph lies on one irreducible plane curve is a polynomial without any smoothness hypothesis (\cref{osq:sa:cor:irreducible}). Every semialgebraic preserver is polynomial
on its two tails, the quotient by the bounded-region preservers being $\Num_1(B)^2$ (\cref{osq:sa:thm:tails,osq:sa:cor:germs}); but for every ordinary
$\mathsf k$ a semialgebraic $C^{\mathsf k}$ preserver agrees on $\Oz$ with no finite family of polynomials (\cref{osq:sa:thm:bumps}). So 22's target
of a piecewise classification with finitely many polynomial pieces is attainable only on the tails, or with algebraic branches as pieces; the
bounded-region preservers are \cref{osq:sa:q:bounded}. The certificate clause of (a) is answered negatively for samples chosen independently of the
coefficients, even for a globally smooth branch of an irreducible quadratic graph (\cref{osq:sa:thm:nosettests}), while a globally smooth semialgebraic
nonpreserver fails on a proper class of inputs (\cref{osq:sa:cor:exceptions,osq:sa:cor:exceptionsmany}). 25 asks for coefficient-adapted certificates
(its Question~12.7), merged into (a): given a quantifier-free algebraic graph description and exact access to its surreal coefficients, can preservation be
certified or refuted by finitely many coefficient-adapted lattice points and finitely many support conditions? 25's comments: its no-set theorem leaves
this adaptive question open, and an answer should distinguish symbolic decidability from the existence of a finite mathematical certificate. 25 also asks
(its Question~12.9), merged into (b), to extend the smooth classification from affine space to semialgebraic manifolds or algebraic varieties with a
specified omnific integral model, and which geometric conditions replace coordinate cofinality and tensor interpolation; 25's comments: the affine proof
does not transplant, since a variety may have few omnific points and no cofinal coordinate lines, and the omnific Diophantine geometry of the repository
\cite{RepoOdg} should be a separate input with its hypotheses audited. The rest of (b), and (c), (d), stay as above. The dynamics report
\cite{RepoDyn} poses a dynamical relative of (a): its reciprocal rational maps have exactly prescribed infinitely large finite periodic points, all in
$\GOz$, and a numerator--denominator presentation with purely infinite Gaussian omnific coefficients, but are deliberately not shown to map $\GOz$ into
itself (\nolinkurl{dyn:rd:thm:omnific}); it asks which polynomial or rational maps preserve $\Oz$ or $\GOz$ on a natural invariant domain while
realizing specified infinite cycles (\nolinkurl{dyn:rd:q:omnific}). Neither is an answer to a clause here.

\begin{question}[The full rational Hahn workspace; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:fullQ}
Let $K_{\Q a}=\hahn k{\Q a}$, with arbitrary reverse well-ordered supports, let $\A(\Q a)$ be its omnific or Gaussian omnific integer part and
$\Pi(\Q a)$ its positive-support ideal. Is $\Pi(\Q a)\IC_{K_{\Q a}}(\A(\Q a))$ radical?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's comments: \cref{osq:rm:thm:pui} answers the bounded-denominator subcase affirmatively, and the obstruction to repeating its
proof is exact: an element of $K_{\Q a}$, and the coefficients of its integrality equation, need not lie in a finite cyclic refinement. A first
intermediate case would allow supports generated by finitely many rationally independent real exponents, with a restriction preventing positive
supports from accumulating at zero. Divisibility of the exponent group alone is not a proof of radicality; the supports of the coefficients must be
controlled as well. For the real pair $K_{\Q a}$ is real closed, so \cref{osq:nf:thm:abstract} would apply if its axiom (ii) held there; the support
$\{a/n:n\ge1\}$ blocks the monomial proof of (ii) (the paragraph after that theorem), and whether (ii) holds is not decided \merge.

\begin{question}[The uncountable Boolean isomorphism type; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:boolean}
Determine the isomorphism types of $\Idem(\mathsf B(\Z a))$ and $\Idem(\mathsf B^{\mathrm{co}}(\Z a))$ for $k=\R$ and $k=\C$. Are there invariants,
beyond atomlessness, cardinality, order density and relative splitting, that distinguish them from familiar Boolean algebras?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's comments: the countable answer of \cref{osq:rm:thm:countable} is a baseline, and one would like to describe the Stone space
directly from compatible places of finite function fields over $T=0$. The explicit family gives $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ points on the coefficient side
(\cref{osq:rm:cor:manyplaces}), but neither a product representation of the ring nor a free presentation of the algebra follows from this count;
countable joins, saturation and automorphisms should be asked separately, and relative splitting is weaker than all of them together. This is the
fixed-cyclic counterpart of \cref{osq:bb:q:structure}, which concerns the proper-class algebra $\Idem(\mathsf B_\R)$; by
\cref{osq:rm:rem:boolboundary} the idempotents of $\mathsf B(\Z a)$ and $\mathsf C(\Z a)$ are the same.

\begin{question}[Arithmetic residue gluing; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:gluing}
Describe concretely the embedding $\mathsf B(\Z a)\hookrightarrow\mathsf B^{\mathrm{co}}(\Z a)$ and the extension
$0\to\mathsf J/T\mathscr B\to\mathsf B(\Z a)\to\mathsf C(\Z a)\to0$. How much of $D$ can be recovered intrinsically from this extension and its
multiplication, without naming the inclusion $D\subseteq k$?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's comments: the residue criterion says which elements of $\mathscr B$ lie in $\NN(\Z a)$, and the task is to organize these
conditions uniformly over all finite fields and all compatible branches. The strict inclusion of \cref{osq:rm:prop:annR} is an intrinsic arithmetic
signal: multiplication by a nilpotent admits coefficients that cannot occur in the arithmetic fibre. A Boolean-power or locally constant description
must keep this nonreduced information, not only the reduced data, for which see \cref{osq:bb:prop:fixedboolean,osq:rm:rem:booleanform}.

\begin{question}[Homological dimensions of the arithmetic fibre; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:arhomology}
What are the weak global and global dimensions of $\mathsf B(\Z a)$? Can the kernels $\bar{\mathsf z}_n^{n-j}\mathsf B^{\mathrm{co}}(\Z a)$ be resolved
over $\mathsf B(\Z a)$ so as to compute a nonzero sequence of higher $\Tor$ groups?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's comments: the infinite dimensions of $\mathsf B^{\mathrm{co}}(\Z a)$ (\cref{osq:rm:thm:periodic}) cannot be pulled back through the
inclusion, since the alternating maps cease to be a resolution over $\mathsf B(\Z a)$ (\cref{osq:rm:prop:annR}); a direct approach would start from
the $\mathsf B(\Z a)$-module structure of $\mathsf B^{\mathrm{co}}(\Z a)$, the modules $\bar{\mathsf z}_n^r\mathsf B^{\mathrm{co}}(\Z a)$ and their relation
modules. This is not the question on projective dimensions of the constant module over the finite-support cores (\cref{osq:hd:q:cores}); those
rings, modules and maps are different.

\begin{question}[The completed coefficient ring; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:completion}
Describe $\widehat{\mathscr B}=\varprojlim_r\mathscr B/T^r\mathscr B$ intrinsically. Is there a useful representation by compatible completed local
valuation rings, and which restricted-product or branch-compatibility conditions are needed?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's comments: by \cref{osq:rm:cor:completion} the arithmetic completion reduces to this problem together with the known first
fibre. With $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ branches over zero, a naive identification with an unrestricted product of local completions needs proof and should
not be assumed, and completion in the integer powers of $T$ should be distinguished from completion for the filtration indexed by all positive
rationals.

\begin{question}[Refinement beyond monomial root maps; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:nonmonomial}
For finite algebraic covers replacing $T=U^m$, which branchwise ramification data determine the kernel on arithmetic fibres? Is there an exact
analogue of \eqref{osq:rm:eq:generalrefine} when different branches have different ramification indices?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's comments: the uniform multiplier $m$ is what makes the threshold a single scalar, and a nonuniform cover needs the full tuple
of branch orders, not only their minimum. Finite normalization and lying over give a concrete formulation, but compatibility with the arithmetic
integer parts must be checked: a map of function fields alone need not induce the desired map of fibres.

\begin{question}[A formal development; 23]\label{osq:rm:q:formal}
Formalize the cyclic nonradicality theorem, the residue criterion and the refinement law in Lean, with an abstract algebraic-function-field layer
separate from the embedding into the constructed surreal field.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 23's plan: first the short argument for $\mathsf z_n$, with finite normalization and one valuation normalized by $v(T)=1$; then
the coefficient-span lemma and the exact ideal test; the Boolean splitting needs further finite-extension and ramification infrastructure, and the
periodic resolution follows once the annihilator identity is available. No declaration has been implemented, and no repository build was run for 23
(\cref{osq:sub:formalization}).

\begin{question}[Choice strength for the omnific ring; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:choice}
Over $\mathsf{GB}$ with choice for sets, does every $(1+\omega^a)\subseteq\Oz$ have a maximal class extension? Does the existence of such extensions for
all $a>0$ imply global choice? What changes when a single value, such as $a=1$, is fixed?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 24's comments: \cref{osq:cr:thm:equivalence} cannot answer this restriction, since its converse builds class polynomial rings whose
variables encode all finite partial choice functions; a first step would be to see whether that compatibility encoding can be interpreted in a fixed
binomial quotient without assuming the global choice class.

\begin{question}[Definable rather than globally selected kernels; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:definable}
Can a nonarithmetic maximal ideal of $\Oz$ be defined in the pure set-theoretic language from a set parameter, in natural models of set theory? Can one
specify a branch of the dyadic algebra for which a definable maximal extension exists?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 24's comments: its uniformity is relative to a chosen global well-order, not parameter-free canonicity; absoluteness and
definability should be studied separately from existence in an expanded class model, and a construction stable under a useful class of universe
extensions would be much stronger than the choice-dependent recursion.

\begin{question}[Are the binomial residue fields algebraically closed?; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:closed}
For a maximal ideal $M\supseteq(1+\omega^a)$, must $\Oz/M$ be algebraically closed? If not, which algebraic extensions occur over it? Ask the same for
$\GOz$.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 24's comments: by \cref{osq:cr:cor:acfiso} a positive answer would identify these residue fields abstractly with $\SC$ in
$\mathsf{GBC}$; the embedded algebraically closed field (\cref{osq:cr:cor:properfield}) supplies roots only for polynomials with coefficients in it; a
concrete test is to understand integral extensions of the binomial quotient and which of their elements descend into its maximal fields, and a first
target is a root-existence theorem for monic polynomials with coefficients in a finite extension of the embedded dyadic and Hahn core. 24 calls this the
most consequential next step.

\begin{question}[Size over the Hahn core; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:relative}
How large can a family algebraically independent over the embedded $\FF_a(i)$ be in a binomial residue field? Can the residue field equal that core, or a
prescribed set-generated extension of it? Which branch choices force additional transcendence?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 24's comments: the explicit core is useful because it is a fixed base for algebraic dependence, not only a cardinal bound; the dyadic
roots are algebraic over it, so the continuum of branch choices is not by itself a transcendence-degree argument.

\begin{question}[Branching beyond the dyadic subalgebra; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:branching}
At one fixed scale $a$, is there a family of distinct maximal class ideals indexed by every set cardinal? Can larger independent idempotent families be
built in $\Qa_a$, and which compatible finite-algebra specializations extend with prescribed residue-field properties?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. The known lower bound at a fixed scale is $2^{\aleph_0}$ (\cref{osq:cr:thm:cantor}). 24's comments: the ordinal family changes the
embedded scale and rescaling identifies the abstract fibres, so it cannot be counted again; new independent equations inside one fibre are needed.
For comparison, 20's fresh-scale splitting (\cref{osq:bb:thm:uniform,osq:bb:thm:free}) builds free Boolean families of every set size in the
normalization fibre $\NN/\Pi\NN$, a different ring \merge.

\begin{question}[Removing one support-closure hypothesis; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:support}
Classify the term-closed prime ideals of $\Oz$ without assuming strong sum-closure, and the strongly sum-closed ones without assuming term-closure. Does
one closure property force the other under a natural additional algebraic or definability condition?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 24's comments: the proof of \cref{osq:cr:thm:termprimes} uses the two properties at different points, one to extract a monomial
support restriction and the other to rebuild a series from its terms; a counterexample or a redundancy theorem would locate the reach of coefficientwise
methods, and neither implication should be assumed.

\begin{question}[Formal verification at the right foundational level; 24]\label{osq:cr:q:formal}
Can the finite-algebra and support-identity package be formalized over the repository's constructed surreal field, with the class-choice theorem
formalized separately in an explicit model of $\mathsf{GB}$?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 24's plan: first the degree and unit lemmas, the geometric multiplier, the monomial inverse certificates, the dyadic idempotents and
the convex truncation kernels; maximal ideals of set rings in a larger Lean universe can then check the algebraic consequences of maximality, but do not
verify the metatheorem over two-sorted $\mathsf{GB}$, since a Lean type is set-sized relative to a larger universe and the strength of global choice must
not be hidden in a universe change; the last step is an explicit syntactic or semantic formalization of the class recursion and the choice equivalence
(\cref{osq:sub:formalization}).

\begin{question}[The optimal differentiability threshold; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:optimal}
For each graph degree $\mathsf D$, determine the least $\mathsf k(\mathsf D)$ such that every globally $C^{\mathsf k(\mathsf D)}$ semialgebraic preserver of a
cofinal discretely ordered ring is polynomial. Is a linear bound in $\mathsf D$ possible, or can polynomial contact force quadratic growth?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open; for $\Oz$, $1+\lfloor(\mathsf D-2)/4\rfloor\le\mathsf s(\mathsf D)\le\mathsf D^2$ and $\mathsf s(1)=1$ (\cref{osq:sa:cor:regularity}).
25's comments: the proof of \cref{osq:sa:thm:degree} bounds the contact order of $Q(X,Y)=0$ with $Y=P(X)$ by $\mathsf D\deg P$, and improving that estimate
under the arithmetic tail constraint is a concrete route; the lower bound is linear in $\mathsf D$ but proves no optimality of $\mathsf D^2$.

\begin{question}[Bounds for full vector graphs; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:multireg}
Given a degree-$\mathsf D$ description of the full graph of a map $E^r\to E^{r'}$, find an explicit regularity threshold in terms of $\mathsf D,r,r'$ without
first using an unspecified quantifier-elimination bound for the scalar coordinate graphs. Can output elimination keep useful dimension-free bounds?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: \cref{osq:sa:thm:smoothmany} gives the dimension-free bound $\mathsf D^2$ for scalar graphs and for vector maps whose
coordinate graphs each have that degree; eliminating the other outputs from one full graph can increase degree, and quantifying that increase is a distinct
problem.

\begin{question}[Bounded-region structure; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:bounded}
Classify the ideal $\operatorname{SA}_{\mathrm b}(\Oz)$ of bounded-region semialgebraic lattice preservers. Which of its elements arise by multiplying a
semialgebraic function over $K_H$ by a multiplier supported in $H^{\uparrow}$, followed by a finite cutoff?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: the exact quotient \cref{osq:sa:cor:germs} reduces the classification of all semialgebraic preservers to this ideal
and a known numerical-polynomial ring; absorption gives a large explicit subclass, not a converse. 25 names this the focused next problem, with regularity
and exponent rank tracked together.

\begin{question}[Multipliers for one algebraic family; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:individual}
For a fixed algebraic branch $\phi$, determine all $c\in\No$ with $c\phi(x)\in\Oz$ on a prescribed omnific interval. Can cancellation in a nonmonomial $c$
allow substantially smaller supports than absorption of all of $K_H$ requires?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: \cref{osq:sa:thm:absorption} answers the uniform field-absorption question exactly and \cref{osq:sa:thm:radical} the
monomial square-root case; the family-specific problem between them is not settled.

\begin{question}[Rank and local flexibility; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:rank}
For a fixed divisible ordered exponent group $\Gamma$, when does its normal-form integer part admit a semialgebraic preserver of a prescribed finite
smoothness order that is not finitely piecewise polynomial?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: a pair $0<a\ll b$ in $\Gamma$ suffices (\cref{osq:sa:prop:setmodel}); its failure in rank one rules out one mechanism
(\cref{osq:sa:prop:rankone}), and necessity for all constructions is not proved.

\begin{question}[Beyond semialgebraicity; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:ominimal}
Which polynomially bounded o-minimal expansions of real closed Hahn fields admit the same cofinal-discrete-ring tail theorem? Under what hypotheses does
global infinite differentiability still continue the tail polynomial through the whole domain?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: the finite-difference part needs polynomial growth, derivative control and eventual monotonicity, and the global step
the appropriate nonflatness theorem; exponential structures need different growth conclusions, and the classical literature \cite{JTW,BMRW} is a guide,
not an automatic transfer.

\begin{question}[Groups of finite-smoothness lattice diffeomorphisms; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:groups}
Study the group of semialgebraic $C^{\mathsf k}$ diffeomorphisms of $\No^r$ preserving $\Oz^r$. How much of it is generated by numerical-polynomial
automorphisms, affine arithmetic maps and the bounded-window shears of \cref{osq:sa:cor:shears}?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: the globally smooth subgroup is polynomial by \cref{osq:sa:thm:smoothmany}, which does not classify its
automorphisms; the finite-smoothness group contains bounded-window elements of Jacobian determinant one, and its relation to the smooth subgroup is
unexplored. The polynomial subgroup is the subject of \cref{osq:ft:q:maps}(c).

\begin{question}[Complex regularity versus real cutoffs; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:complex}
Find minimal regularity assumptions under which a real-semialgebraic lattice preserver of $\GOz$ satisfying the Cauchy--Riemann equations is polynomial.
Can the $C^\infty$ hypothesis of \cref{osq:sa:cor:holomorphic} be reduced uniformly at fixed graph complexity?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: the shear counterexamples are not holomorphic, so they do not settle it, and a proof should stay within an explicit
surreal differential framework rather than import complex analytic continuation.

\begin{question}[Arithmetic invisibility inside the purely infinite ideal; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:invisibility}
Classify the semialgebraic maps whose lattice values all lie in $\Pi$, modulo bounded-region modifications. More generally, prescribe the ordinary
constant-term map on $\Oz^r$ and determine the allowed bounded-window deformations.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: for smooth maps the numerical-polynomial decomposition and coefficientwise constant terms answer it
(\cref{osq:sa:cor:explicit}); finite regularity brings in the radical examples, whose geometry is invisible to every output constant term.

\begin{question}[Formal verification; 25]\label{osq:sa:q:formal}
Formalize the cofinal tail-extrapolation lemma, semialgebraic finite-difference rigidity and convex-support absorption, and combine them with the
repository's actual omnific ring. Which part of real closed semialgebraic calculus can be reused without new axioms?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 25's comments: the core algebraic identities are finite and good early targets; the delicate obligations are semialgebraic Rolle and
monotonicity over arbitrary real closed fields, the class-to-set support reduction, and the exact support of a rational-power Hahn expansion
(\cref{osq:sub:formalization}).

\begin{question}[Flat extensions of cones; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:flatext}
For pointed cones $\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr C'$ in the same rational space, characterize flatness of $A_{\mathscr C}\to A_{\mathscr C'}$. Which new exponent
comparisons force the two-ray obstruction of \cref{osq:pc:thm:nonflat}?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: a necessary condition is that no newly admitted quotient of distinct old ray monomials creates the forbidden unit-constant
relation; whether a finite set of such comparisons suffices, or higher syzygies add obstructions when all two-ray tests pass, is to be decided.

\begin{question}[Recognition without named monomials; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:recognition}
Does the abstract ring $A_{\mathscr C}$, with $D$ named but no grading, determine the face lattice of $\mathscr C$? When must an isomorphism preserve the
geometric radical ideals?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: \cref{osq:pc:cor:reconstruct} solves only the marked version; an unmarked theorem needs an intrinsic characterization of the
coefficient-full geometric ideals, which connects these invariants to the repository's embedding and automorphism program.

\begin{question}[Infinite-support extensions; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:infinite}
Which Hahn-type completions of $A_{\mathscr C}$ keep the principal exhaustion of each $I_F$, the detector formula and the finite flat resolutions?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: the issue is whether one positive shift can be subtracted from all exponents of a series; finite supports allow a minimum over
finitely many inequalities, while an infinite support can approach a boundary face with no uniform inward margin, so a theorem must impose a support
condition excluding this or replace principal exhaustion.

\begin{question}[Exponent-density hypotheses; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:density}
Replace $\Q^d$ by a subgroup $\Gamma\subseteq\R^d$. Which conditions on $\Gamma\cap F$ for each face are sufficient, or necessary, for flat face ideals and for
\eqref{osq:pc:eq:mainface}?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: the proof uses countable sequences in relative interiors tending to zero and enough subtraction stability, not every rational
exponent; comparison with the dense-subgroup orthant case of Geist--Miller \cite[Section~4]{GeistMiller} should separate the existence of a flat resolution
from the telescope bound on projective dimension.

\begin{question}[Beyond polyhedral cones; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:nonpolyhedral}
Can an infinite face poset give a usable analogue of the join-homology formula? How do the number of faces, the cofinality of inward shifts and homological
dimension interact for nonpolyhedral cones?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: finite-label cancellation is no longer automatic, and finite supports do not force finitely many labels globally; locally
polyhedral cones and increasing unions of rational cones are controlled first cases.

\begin{question}[Arithmetic rings beyond principal ideal domains; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:arithmetic}
For a general domain $D\subseteq K$, determine the flat dimensions over $A_{\mathscr C}$ of the modules acting through $D$.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: \cref{osq:pc:thm:arithmetic} uses the torsion theory and flatness of torsion-free modules over a principal ideal domain;
over a non-Pr\"ufer domain further homology of $D$ survives, and a theorem should separate the cone contribution from the $D$-module contribution without
simply adding dimensions where torsion removes the tail.

\begin{question}[Efficient reduced resolutions; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:algorithms}
Can the top join homology and a detector certificate be computed without all $2^r$ subsets of generators? Can the reduced differentials be chosen canonically
or functorially?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: its program favours auditability over efficiency; for face-prime quotients the disjoint-face formula already replaces subset
enumeration by a maximum over the face poset, and general antichains may admit discrete-Morse or interval reductions compatible with
\cref{osq:pc:lem:cancellation}, the lcm-lattice techniques being classical \cite{GPW}.

\begin{question}[Characteristic-sensitive examples; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:characteristic}
Which finite face antichains have join complexes whose homology depends on the characteristic of $K$, and how small can such a cone and antichain be?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: \cref{osq:pc:cor:squarefree} gives a route through torsion in squarefree monomial topology; the omnific applications are in
characteristic zero, and a minimal example would show which parts of the arbitrary-field theorem carry arithmetic information.

\begin{question}[Derived structure beyond self-$\Tor$; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:derived}
Describe the derived restriction along $A_{\mathscr C}\to A_{\mathscr C}/\mathfrak r_{\mathcal F}$, including the subcategory invisible to tensoring with the
quotient and any compact-generation properties.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's comments: the homological epimorphism is proved (\cref{osq:pc:thm:homological}); a recollement or compactness statement needs more
hypotheses and proofs, and the contrast between vanishing self-$\Tor$ and nonzero detector $\Tor$ is a starting point, not a substitute for that analysis.

\begin{question}[A staged formalization; 26]\label{osq:pc:q:formal}
Formalize the disjoint-face formula, separating finite combinatorics, filtered monomial ideals and the embedding into the surreal field.
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 26's plan: encode finite rational cones and joins; prove principal exhaustion; prove the simplex and cap calculations; formalize finite scalar
cancellation; then import the normal-form embedding. The equational nonflatness theorem is a small independent target, the finite relation criterion being in
Mathlib (\texttt{Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.EquationalCriterion}); 26 supplies no Lean code (\cref{osq:sub:formalization}).

\begin{question}[The exact Boolean algebra; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:boolean}
For the hull of \cref{osq:hb:prop:hull}, determine $\Idem(\mathscr G)$ up to isomorphism. Is it atomless? Can $\mathsf X$ have isolated points? For
$\kappa=\aleph_0$, can the construction be refined so that $\mathsf X$ is the Cantor space?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: a free subalgebra of rank $\kappa$ and $|\mathsf X|=2^\kappa$ decide none of these; a first step is to classify which further
pointed \'etale neighbourhoods produce idempotents outside the algebra generated by the $\hat e_\alpha$. Compare \cref{osq:bb:q:structure,osq:rm:q:boolean} for
the Boolean algebras of 20's and 23's fibres.

\begin{question}[Dependence on the hull; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:hull}
How far do the isomorphism type of $\mathscr G$, or the homeomorphism type of $\mathsf X$, depend on the choices of clearing and division in the hull? Is
there a natural equivalence class of such spaces attached to a seed field?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: the theorem is existential; it keeps the cardinal and the seed but proves no canonical minimal hull or uniqueness of its
local algebra.

\begin{question}[Enlarging an integer part; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:enlargement}
For induced omnific integer parts $B\subseteq B'$ with compatible localizations $\mathfrak L\to\mathfrak L'$, when is the map of generic henselian fibres
injective, and when do branches merge or appear?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: the splitter atoms survive every global normalization witness, which protects the certified family but not idempotents
created by unrelated \'etale neighbourhoods.

\begin{question}[Normalization versus henselization; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:normalization}
Relate the reduced normalization fibre $\IC_{\mathbb E}(\mathfrak L)/\sqrt{\mathfrak n\IC_{\mathbb E}(\mathfrak L)}$ to the Stone space $\mathsf X$. Can the
finite-pattern argument give an explicit correspondence between normalization choices and henselian minimal primes?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: a solution should separate residue-field extensions from geometric splitting and account for the forced passage from
$\mathbb E$ to $\mathbb E[i]$; a map on the whole normalization fibre is stronger than the finite atom survival proved. The full-class fibre
$\NN/\Pi\NN\cong\overline\Z[\Idem]$ (\cref{osq:nf:thm:boolean}) is the class analogue of that normalization fibre \merge.

\begin{question}[Specialization in the local spectrum; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:spectrum}
Determine the prime chains between the $2^\kappa$ minimal primes and the maximal ideal of $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}$. Which Krull dimensions occur among
hulls of cardinality $\kappa$, and which specialization patterns can be prescribed?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: the generic fibre is zero-dimensional, which says nothing about the dimension of the local ring; branching and dimension
should be studied separately.

\begin{question}[The valuation components; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:valuation}
What are the value groups, residue fields and internal topologies of the connected components of $\operatorname{RZ}(\mathfrak L)$? Can valuations realizing
all explicit Boolean assignments be built directly from the scale data?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: \cref{osq:hb:cor:rz} counts components through an external theorem; a direct valuative realization would explain how
order-infinite elements acquire positive value at these non-order-convex centres.

\begin{question}[Mixed-characteristic constant-term primes; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:mixed}
Replace $\Pi_{\mathbb E}$ by $\ct^{-1}(p\Z)\cap B_{\mathbb E}$ for an ordinary prime $p$. What remains of maximal branching, forced complexification and the
strict Galois product, and what changes at $p=2$?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: the quadratic formulas use $2$ and $16$ as units after rationalization, and at a mixed-characteristic centre the residue
extension and the completion differ, so the proofs do not transfer. By \cref{osq:thm:quotients} the corresponding ideal of $\Oz$ is $p\Oz=p\Z+\Pi$, which
already contains $\Pi$ \merge.

\begin{question}[Finite \'etale algebras before localization; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:unlocalized}
Classify finite \'etale algebras over $B_{\mathbb E}$ and compare their restrictions to the rational constant-term localization and the ordinary prime
localizations. Is there a useful arithmetic gluing description?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: $\operatorname{Fin\acute Et}(\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h})\simeq\operatorname{Fin\acute Et}(\Q)$ is henselian local algebra, not a
classification over $B_{\mathbb E}$ (\cref{osq:hb:prop:etale}).

\begin{question}[Birthday-bounded realizations; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:birthday}
For which ordinals $\lambda$ can the hull be built inside the surreals born before $\lambda$? How do closure requirements, regularity or large-cardinal
hypotheses improve bounds on $\lambda$?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: one seed can have a very long sign expansion, and a fresh support bound may leave a chosen cutoff; controlled birthday
realizations would connect the local algebra to the foundational reports without confusing cardinality with birthday.

\begin{question}[Compatible class-level geometry; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:class}
Can the directed system of set-sized omnific augmentation rings and their henselizations be organized into a class-sized geometric object without treating
the class of all primes as a set? Which invariants are stable?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: an answer must state its foundations and transition maps; 27 avoids class spectra and class ultrafilters. 24's maximal
class ideals (\cref{osq:cr:thm:krull}) show one foundation, global choice, in which class ideals of $\Oz$ can be built \merge.

\begin{question}[Higher invariants and descent; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:higher}
How far do finite-partition methods extend to higher $K$-theory, derived categories and cohomological invariants of $\mathscr G$ and
$\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}$? Which invariants of $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm h}$ become locally constant after passage to $\mathscr G$?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's comments: filtered colimits and product formulas are natural starting points; only $K_0(\mathscr G)$ and the finite projectives are
proved.

\begin{question}[Formal verification of the branch bridge; 27]\label{osq:hb:q:formal}
Can the monic certificates, the support projection and the survival of finite branches be formalized in Lean and connected to a library construction of
henselization and Boolean spectra?
\end{question}
\emph{Status.} Open. 27's plan: first \cref{osq:hb:lem:allbranches}, with its quantification over every denominator (a proof of the quadratic identity alone
would miss the difficulty); then, in order, the finite quadratic identities, monic certificates, support projection, survival under localization, the hull,
and henselization, spectra and cardinality, which need general commutative-algebra and topology infrastructure beyond the surreal normal-form interface
(\cref{osq:sub:formalization}).

\section{Verification record and formalization routes}\label{osq:sec:provenance}

\subsection{Finite checks}\label{osq:sub:checks}

for the eight merges on copies (Python~3.14.4, SymPy~1.14.0) and reproduce the recorded outputs, up to line
endings, the recorded Python version, for 18 the recorded time stamp and for 23 its hash of the unshipped manuscript.

These checks catch sign, index and coefficient errors in finite special cases. None of them
verifies an infinite support, a class-size argument, a cardinal computation, the existence of a
maximal ideal, an $\Ext$ computation, a primality statement, or novelty; those rest on the written
proofs (all sources). The merge results were not machine-checked. For the second merge an independent exact
computation, not shipped, rechecked \cref{osq:hd:thm:boolean} in $1{,}626$ cases (multidegree and subset $F$, including
every proper $F$, over $\Q\subset\Q(\sqrt2)$ in ranks up to $3$) and the formulas of \cref{osq:tn:cor:alldegrees} for
$d\le8$, $n\le12$; like the shipped checks it verifies finite cases only. For the third merge, independent exact computations, not
shipped, rechecked the Pell matrix, the multiplication kernels and self-$\Tor$ endpoints for $r\le5$, the irreducibility of $X^r-(1+i)$ over
$\Q(i)$ for $r\le6$ and five $\mathrm{GL}_2(\Z)$ cases (17); the composition obstruction of \cref{osq:or:thm:composition} in 27 random cases and
the formula for $\eta_f$ (18); the idempotent identities, the Catalan expansion and 36 random cases of the lifting bound (19); and the sizes
of the Gaussian certificates compared in \cref{osq:or:prop:gausstest} for $n\le3$, $d\le5$. For the fourth merge an independent exact
computation, not shipped, rechecked in 18 checks the certificate \eqref{osq:bb:eq:splitter}, the values of $\sigma_\pm$, the many-branch identity
of \cref{osq:bb:thm:rank}, the simple zeros used for the square classes, and the identities behind \cref{osq:bb:prop:candidates}. For the
fifth merge an independent exact computation, not shipped, rechecked in 78 checks the converse formula of \cref{osq:da:thm:injection} in 12
cases, the exponent identities behind it, the Koszul transition identity, the ranks of $\Tor_2$ and $\operatorname{Ind}_2$ and the
discriminants of the four orders, and the product rank for $\Q(\sqrt2),\Q(\sqrt3)$; like 21's checks it proves no infinite $\Ext$
nonvanishing. For the sixth merge an independent exact computation, not shipped, rechecked in 101 checks the resultant and the partial fractions of
\cref{osq:ft:ex:resultant}, the counts after \cref{osq:ft:thm:certificate} and the comparison of \cref{osq:ft:rem:probes} for $m\le4$, $d\le5$, the
bound \eqref{osq:ft:eq:sharpD} in twelve random trivariate cases, the inverse shears of \cref{osq:ft:ex:shear}, the two Gaussian denominators and the
coefficients of \cref{osq:ft:ex:integers}; it proves no statement about infinite supports. For the seventh merge 23's program was rerun on a
copy: all $18{,}040$ assertions pass in the same 12 categories, and the rewritten record differs from the shipped one only in the Python
version and in its hash of the manuscript, which is \texttt{null} because the manuscript is not shipped beside the program (and, on Windows, in
line endings). An independent exact
computation, not shipped, rechecked in $2{,}642$ checks (most of them the exponent inequality of axiom (ii) used in \cref{osq:rm:rem:puiabstract})
the relations \eqref{osq:rm:eq:zn} for $n\le7$ and \eqref{osq:rm:eq:splitter}, the refinement certificates of \cref{osq:rm:thm:explicitrefinement}, the
Laurent coefficients and the full-class factorization of \cref{osq:rm:ex:sqrt}, the residues of the Boolean words of \cref{osq:rm:thm:cardinality} modulo
$T$ for three parameters with the squarefreeness of their radicands, and the cancellation identity behind \cref{osq:rm:thm:annC}; like 23's program it
verifies no integral closure, place or cardinality. For the eighth merge 24's and 25's programs (standard library only) were rerun on copies with an
explicit output path (Python~3.14.4): 24 passed all $133{,}770$ assertions in the same six groups and 25 all $1{,}578$ in the same 18 groups, and the
rewritten records differ from \texttt{data/24-class-residues-verification.json} and \texttt{data/25-semialgebraic-smoothness-verification.json} only in the
recorded Python version (3.14.4 for 3.13.5) and, on Windows, in line endings; 24's shipped \texttt{.txt} record is byte-identical to its JSON record.
Neither program proves a class recursion, an infinite Hahn identity, a semialgebraic calculus theorem or a proper-class statement. An independent exact
computation (SymPy), not shipped, rechecked in $300$ checks the identification of 24's first idempotents with 07's modulo $\xi_2^4+1$
(\cref{osq:cr:rem:dyadic}), the squarefreeness and absence of real roots of $T^{2^n}+1$ for $n\le5$, finite geometric remainders behind
\eqref{osq:cr:eq:telescope}, the Boolean-ring criterion of \cref{osq:cr:rem:ultrafilters} for pairs in the algebra of subsets of a four-element set, the
coefficients $\frac12$ and $-\frac18$ of \eqref{osq:sa:eq:testfailure} for $b=1,\dots,4$, the constant of the $\mathsf k$th derivative in the proof of
\cref{osq:sa:thm:bumps} for $\mathsf k\le6$ with the degree count of \cref{osq:sa:cor:regularity}, and the vanishing orders behind
\cref{osq:sa:rem:exceptionsnecessary}; it verifies no class recursion, infinite support or semialgebraic calculus. 26's and 27's programs were also rerun on
copies (Python~3.14.4, SymPy~1.14.0): 26 passed all $52{,}080$ assertions with the same counts ($188$, $1{,}329$, $56$, $2{,}457$) and rewrote a record, beside
itself, identical to \texttt{data/26-face-topology-verification\_results.json} except for the elapsed time; 27 passed all $5{,}760$ assertions in the same eight
groups, and its record, written only with \texttt{--output}, equals \texttt{data/27-henselian-branching-verification.json} up to line endings on Windows.
Neither verifies a filtered colimit, a localization denominator, a prime or a cardinality. An independent exact computation (SymPy), not shipped,
rechecked in $2{,}726$ checks the multiplicities \eqref{osq:pc:eq:facebetti} and the flat dimension $\mu_{\mathscr C}(F)$ for every proper nonzero face of the
cones over a square and a cube, by computing the reduced homology of every join complex $\mathsf K_{<G}$ directly, the square-cone multiplicities of the
examples, the splitter identity and the one-radical factorization of \cref{osq:hb:rem:oneradical} with its six Laurent coefficients, the identity
$\jmath^2=-1$ of \cref{osq:hb:prop:complex} and the inverse of the Gaussian decomposition; it verifies no colimit, detector module or henselization.

\subsection{Formalization routes}\label{osq:sub:formalization}
The source-era assertion that the repository has no omnific module is now obsolete.
The ledger \texttt{docs/FORMALIZATION.md} maps the actual omnific and Gaussian rings,
their retractions, degree and unit laws, common-divisor support arguments and the
quadratic definition of the purely infinite ideals through the sibling report's labels.
This shared material does not prove the full-class quotient theorem or the cardinal
threshold results here. The following routes remain proposals for those statements.
First formalize the scaled-field collision
lemma and the separation lemma, which need no surreals (06, 04, 07). Then the countable telescope in a
set-sized Hahn workspace, with its two support inequalities, proved coefficientwise and not by
convergence of partial sums (04, 06, 07, 08, 10). The set-sized criteria
(\cref{osq:thm:criterion,osq:thm:coinitial}) avoid proper-class syntax and are good first targets (08). The full-class theorem needs an explicit universe interface in which the target and the collision
index are small and the exponent class supplies smaller scales below every small support; a
universe-polymorphic theorem about an arbitrary field does not supply them (04, 08, 10, 11). For the
constructions, the finite-coordinate invariant of 08 must be preserved through field generation,
real closure and truncation, and the module bound at a cardinal must use cyclic quotients or the
direct collision, not an endomorphism ring (08, 06). The homological part comes last, over set-sized
rings only (06). For 07's quotient, the support characterization of $\Oz[\omega^{-a}]$ and the exact
binomial kernel should be kept separate from the finite Chinese-remainder algebra. The repository's
small-normal-form modules (\texttt{SmallNormalForm.lean}, \texttt{SmallNormalFormTruncation.lean},
\texttt{SmallNormalFormEvaluation.lean}, \texttt{SignSequenceValuationBalls.lean}, see
\cite{RepoBridge}) are possible prerequisites (04); they are not a certificate for any result here.
The later manuscripts add three proposals. 12 would define its cores as subrings of a monoid algebra cut out by the
constant-coefficient predicate, with the directed-union equality, exactness of the finite-support simplex complex and the
degreewise classification of \cref{osq:hd:thm:boolean} as the main obligations, and the surreal embedding last. 14 would
start from an abstract domain $A=D\oplus P$ with $P$ a $k$-linear ideal in which every element is a product of two, a
hypothesis the finite-support model satisfies. 16 separates a finite part (simple-root recursion, centering, the leading-term
argument, finite differences), a Hahn part (the block embedding) and an actual-surreal part (a common set-sized exponent
workspace and a fresh exponent). The third batch adds three more. 17 separates a finite layer (saturated lattices, constant kernels,
scalar multipliers and coefficient product matrices over a principal ideal domain), a support layer (the small-family gap and the
union of principal ideals) and a homological layer over the set-sized models only. 18 would formalize the cluster theorem for an
abstract discretely ordered ring and specialize it through the normal-form bridge. 19 would formalize the determinant contraction over
any ring with a retraction, radicality under power divisibility, saturation, the root-forcing estimate, the spectral projectors and the
doubling, and keep the class representation theorem and its ultrafilter foundation separate. 20 proposes its set-sized rank extension
(\cref{osq:bb:thm:rank}) as a first target: Hahn coefficient projection, the finite determinant certificate for radical membership, iterated Hahn
fields and the presentation and specialization of a multiquadratic algebra, all over set-sized ordered groups; the full-surreal theorem needs
in addition the normal-form bridge, a bound above a set of exponents and universe management, and the class-ultrafilter representations
should stay a separate foundational module. The fifth batch adds one. 21 would formalize its dimension theorem on the finite-support monoid
algebra before any surreal embedding: the face ideals, the coefficientwise simplex contraction, the Koszul transitions, the mapping cone and
the last $\Hom$ differential, with the nonvanishing lemma that a finitely supported element cannot have prescribed nonzero coefficients at
infinitely many distinct exponents; its second part would start from an abstract ring $D\oplus\Pi$ with $k\oplus\Pi$, a common positive
monomial factor and a flat tail, whose instantiation at the class rings is a separate obligation. The sixth batch adds one. 22 proposes a small
extension of the repository's Hahn layer: the order embedding $(n,g)\mapsto nb+g$ on lexicographically ordered blocks, reverse well-ordering and local
finiteness of the Laurent image, preservation of multiplication, the nonnegative-support detector, the resultant degree bound with the grid lemma, and
the explicit deceptive function, with the proper-class conclusions proved through an explicit small-set bounding interface; a finite-rank toy model
would not establish the full claims (\cref{osq:ft:q:certificates}(f)). The seventh batch adds one. 23 would first prove its $\mathsf z_n$ argument from
finite normalization and one valuation, then the coefficient-span lemma and the exact ideal test, with an abstract algebraic-function-field layer
separate from the embedding into the surreal field; the Boolean splitting needs further ramification infrastructure, and the periodic resolution
follows from the annihilator identity (\cref{osq:rm:q:formal}). The eighth batch adds two. 24 would first verify the degree and unit lemmas, the
geometric multiplier, the monomial inverse certificates, the dyadic idempotents and the convex truncation kernels over the constructed surreal field, and
formalize the class recursion and the choice equivalence separately, in an explicit model of $\mathsf{GB}$, without hiding global choice in a change of
universe (\cref{osq:cr:q:formal}). 25 would start from the cofinal tail extrapolation, semialgebraic finite-difference rigidity and convex-support
absorption, with semialgebraic Rolle and monotonicity over arbitrary real closed fields, the class-to-set support reduction and the exact support of a
rational-power Hahn expansion as the delicate obligations (\cref{osq:sa:q:formal}). 26 would encode finite rational cones and joins, principal
exhaustion, the simplex and cap calculations and scalar cancellation before the surreal embedding, with the equational nonflatness theorem as a small
separate target (\cref{osq:pc:q:formal}); 27 would start with the survival of every finite branch under localization (\cref{osq:hb:q:formal}). None was executed.
